source.title: Mod p points on Shimura varieties of abelian type
source.venue: Journal of the American Mathematical Society30(3)(2017),819–914
source.version: Author99-page version, dated20160827; author publication list and Crossref verify the publication identity, not text identity with the96-page journal version.
readSections: All99 pages: introduction, §§1.1–1.4,2.1–2.3,3.1–3.8,4.1–4.6,Errata E.1–E.7 and references.

summary: Kisin proves the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture, up to a twist by a cocycle, for the mod p points of Shimura varieties of abelian type at hyperspecial level (p > 2): each isogeny class has the form predicted by an admissible morphism, and every isogeny class contains a point lifting to a special point. The paper also corrects §1.5 and (3.3.9) of Kisin's 2010 integral-models paper. Complete after the independent review REV-PAPER-KISIN-17 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03): 297 items; 107 mistakes recorded (74 misprints, 19 gaps, 14 errors), including the corrections the paper prints to Kisin 2010 and, new, that the definition in (3.6.1) admits ramified twists, so that Lemma 3.6.2(2),(3), Corollary 3.6.4 and Proposition 3.6.10 fail as printed when G^der is not simply connected (the fix is to the definition), that Corollary (2.3.5) fails at non-neat level over small fields, and that Theorem 4.6.7 as printed omits p > 2. Not formalised.

    (H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k) :
    reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty k H ↔
      Algebra.Smooth k H ∧
        geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty k H.obj ∧

structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

variable (A) in
/-- The canonical `DividedPowers` structure on the zero ideal -/

class MonoidalCategory (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v} C] extends MonoidalCategoryStruct C where
  tensorHom_def {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : C} (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (g : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) :
    f ⊗ₘ g = (f ▷ X₂) ≫ (Y₁ ◁ g) := by
      cat_disch
  /-- Tensor product of identity maps is the identity: `𝟙 X₁ ⊗ₘ 𝟙 X₂ = 𝟙 (X₁ ⊗ X₂)` -/
  id_tensorHom_id : ∀ X₁ X₂ : C, 𝟙 X₁ ⊗ₘ 𝟙 X₂ = 𝟙 (X₁ ⊗ X₂) := by cat_disch
  /--
  Composition of tensor products is tensor product of compositions:
  `(f₁ ⊗ₘ f₂) ≫ (g₁ ⊗ₘ g₂) = (f₁ ≫ g₁) ⊗ₘ (f₂ ≫ g₂)`
  -/
  tensorHom_comp_tensorHom :
    ∀ {X₁ Y₁ Z₁ X₂ Y₂ Z₂ : C} (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) (g₁ : Y₁ ⟶ Z₁) (g₂ : Y₂ ⟶ Z₂),
      (f₁ ⊗ₘ f₂) ≫ (g₁ ⊗ₘ g₂) = (f₁ ≫ g₁) ⊗ₘ (f₂ ≫ g₂) := by
    cat_disch
  whiskerLeft_id : ∀ (X Y : C), X ◁ 𝟙 Y = 𝟙 (X ⊗ Y) := by
    cat_disch
  id_whiskerRight : ∀ (X Y : C), 𝟙 X ▷ Y = 𝟙 (X ⊗ Y) := by
    cat_disch
  /-- Naturality of the associator isomorphism: `(f₁ ⊗ₘ f₂) ⊗ₘ f₃ ≃ f₁ ⊗ₘ (f₂ ⊗ₘ f₃)` -/
  associator_naturality :
    ∀ {X₁ X₂ X₃ Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C} (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) (f₃ : X₃ ⟶ Y₃),
      ((f₁ ⊗ₘ f₂) ⊗ₘ f₃) ≫ (α_ Y₁ Y₂ Y₃).hom = (α_ X₁ X₂ X₃).hom ≫ (f₁ ⊗ₘ (f₂ ⊗ₘ f₃)) := by
    cat_disch
  /--
  Naturality of the left unitor, commutativity of `𝟙_ C ⊗ X ⟶ 𝟙_ C ⊗ Y ⟶ Y` and `𝟙_ C ⊗ X ⟶ X ⟶ Y`
  -/
  leftUnitor_naturality :
    ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), 𝟙_ _ ◁ f ≫ (λ_ Y).hom = (λ_ X).hom ≫ f := by
    cat_disch
  /--

items.name: Witt-vector coefficient carrier
items.statement: For prime p and perfect field k of characteristic p use the existing p-typical Witt vectors W(k), with coefficient sequence indexed by natural numbers; its fraction field supplies L. This item is only the coefficient carrier, not a crystalline site.

uses.where: §§1–4, imported foundational carrier in the limited scope stated; consumers PAPER-KISIN-17/D01
uses.how: For p>2 and a complete Noetherian local R with perfect residue k, W_hat(R) is the Zink subring W(k)⊕W_hat(m_R), where the second summand consists of Witt coordinates tending m_R-adically to zero; I_R is the kernel of W_hat(R)→R.
A frame is (S,I,φ,φ1) with I+pS⊂Jac(S), φ a Frobenius lift modulo p, φ1:I→S φ-semilinear with generating image, and φ|_I=pφ1; strict maps preserve these maps and ideals.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin coefficient frame
items.statement: Assume p > 2. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], K/K_0 a finite totally ramified extension with ring of integers O_K, K̄ an algebraic closure of K and G_K = Gal(K̄/K). Fix a uniformiser π ∈ K with Eisenstein polynomial E(u) ∈ W[u]. Put 𝔖 = W[[u]] with the Frobenius φ that is σ on W and sends u to u^p, and let O_E be the p-adic completion of 𝔖_(p). Let S be the p-adic completion of the divided-power envelope of W[u] with respect to the kernel of W[u] → O_K, u ↦ π, with the Frobenius that is σ on W and sends u to u^p. S is an 𝔖-algebra via u ↦ u, W is an S-algebra via u ↦ 0, and 𝔖 → K is u ↦ π.
items.locator: §1.1 opening (p. 5: standing assumption p > 2); (1.1.1) (p. 6: k, W, K_0, K, O_K, G_K, π, E(u), 𝔖 = W[[u]], φ, O_E); (1.1.5) (p. 7: the divided-power ring S)

items.name: Finite free Frobenius module and height one
items.statement: Mod^φ_{/𝔖} is the category of finite free 𝔖-modules 𝔐 with a Frobenius-semilinear isomorphism 1⊗φ: φ*(𝔐)[1/E(u)] ≅ 𝔐[1/E(u)]. BT^φ_{/𝔖} is the full subcategory of those 𝔐 for which 1⊗φ maps φ*(𝔐) into 𝔐 with image containing E(u)𝔐. For i ∈ Z, Fil^i φ*(𝔐) := (1⊗φ)^{-1}(E(u)^i 𝔐) ∩ φ*(𝔐). Mod^φ_{/O_E} is the category of finite free O_E-modules M with an isomorphism φ*(M) ≅ M, and 𝔐 ↦ O_E ⊗_𝔖 𝔐 is a functor Mod^φ_{/𝔖} → Mod^φ_{/O_E}.

items.statement: The functor 𝔐 of (1.1.2) induces an exact equivalence 𝔐: (p-div/O_K) → BT^φ_{/𝔖}, 𝒢 ↦ 𝔐(𝒢) := 𝔐(T_p𝒢*(−1)). items.name: Étale criterion for adaptedness
items.statement: Assume the setting of (1.1.11): 𝒢 over k, φ-invariant (s_{α,0}) ⊂ D(𝒢)(W)^⊗ defining a reductive G_W, and a finite free Z_p-module U with U ⊗_{Z_p} W ≅ D(𝒢)(W) and s_{α,0} ∈ U^⊗. A deformation 𝒢̃ of 𝒢 to O_K is G_W-adapted if and only if, via the p-adic comparison isomorphism D(𝒢̃)(W) ⊗_W B_cris ≅ T_p𝒢̃*(−1) ⊗_{Z_p} B_cris, the s_{α,0} correspond to tensors s_α ∈ T_p𝒢̃^⊗ which define a reductive subgroup of GL(T_p𝒢̃). If this holds, there is a W-linear isomorphism (1.1.14) D(𝒢)(W) ≅ T_p𝒢̃*(−1) ⊗_{Z_p} W taking s_{α,0} to s_α. (The 'if' direction is [Ki 2, Prop. 1.5.11]. For (1.1.14) the proof cites [Ki 2, 1.4.3(3)], which here is (1.1.7) and needs k separably closed, or G_{Z_p} connected and k finite; see the new gap.)
proofSteps: Construct universal rational étale tensors; use connectedness and one integral fiber to obtain integrality and the reductive frame, then compare filtrations.

items.name: Relative crystalline comparison after the period
items.statement: (1.1.16) For R as in (1.1.15) and a p-divisible group 𝒢 over R with T_p(𝒢) := Hom_{R̄}(Q_p/Z_p, 𝒢), the map T_p(𝒢) ⊗_{Z_p} A_cris(R) → Hom_{A_cris(R)}(D(𝒢)(A_cris(R)), A_cris(R)) becomes an isomorphism after inverting t ∈ A_cris = A_cris(W) [Fa 2, p. 114]. Lemma (1.1.17): let 𝒢̃_{R_G} be the universal p-divisible group over Spec R_G (R_G as in (1.1.10), in the setting of (1.1.13)). items.name: Explicit adapted lift with chosen cocharacter
items.statement: In the setting of (1.1.11), with μ_0, υ_0 and b = h·p^{υ_0} (h ∈ G_W(W)) as in Lemma (1.1.12) and its proof: put 𝔐 = σ^{-1*}(D(𝒢)(W)) ⊗_W 𝔖, so that φ*(𝔐) ≅ D(𝒢)(W) ⊗_W 𝔖 and the s_{α,0} ∈ U^⊗ lie in 𝔐^⊗ and φ*(𝔐)^⊗. Let μ be μ_0 viewed in G_𝔖 and c = σ^{-1}(b)μ_0(E(0)). Then c ∈ G_W(W), and the map 1⊗φ given by φ*(𝔐) --c·μ^{-1}(E(u))--> φ*(𝔐) ≅ 𝔐 (the last map induced by the identity on U) makes 𝔐 an object of BT^φ_{/𝔖}. The corresponding p-divisible group 𝒢̃ over O_K (via (1.1.6)) is a deformation of 𝒢, the filtration on ℳ(𝔐) = D(𝒢̃)(S) is induced by μ^{-1}, 𝒢̃ is G_W-adapted, and the s_{α,0} correspond to s_α ∈ T_p𝒢̃^⊗ defining a reductive subgroup. In particular G_W-adapted deformations exist over every O_K.

items.name: Admissible filtration gives an adapted isogenous lift
items.statement: In the setting of (1.1.11), with μ_0, υ_0 as in (1.1.12) and D(𝒢) := D(𝒢)(W), let μ: G_m → G_K be a cocharacter defined over K and conjugate to μ_0 such that μ^{-1} induces an admissible filtration on D(𝒢)_K := D(𝒢)(W) ⊗_W K. Then there exist a finite extension K'/K with residue field k', a p-divisible group 𝒢̃' over O_{K'}, and a quasi-isogeny θ: 𝒢 → 𝒢' := 𝒢̃' ⊗_{O_{K'}} k' (over k') such that: (1) θ identifies the filtration on D(𝒢')_{K'} given by 𝒢̃' with the filtration on D(𝒢)_{K'} induced by μ^{-1}; (2) θ identifies D(𝒢') with g·D(𝒢) for some g with g^{-1}bσ(g) ∈ G(O)p^{υ_0}G(O). Here the printed text has g ∈ G(L) and O = O_L; the proof gives g ∈ G(W(k')[1/p]) and O = W(k'). (3) Viewing s_{α,0} ∈ D(𝒢')^⊗ via θ, 𝒢̃' is gG_{W(k')}g^{-1}-adapted, where gG_{W(k')}g^{-1} is the stabiliser of the s_{α,0} in D(𝒢')^⊗. (The proof needs k separably closed, or G_{Z_p} connected and k finite; see the new gap.)
proofSteps: Use the crystalline/admissible representation correspondence and Wintenberger tensor-frame theorem, choose the integral lattice, then apply the étale adaptedness criterion.

items.name: Frame of an F̄_p-algebra and of a morphism
items.statement: Let R be an F̄_p-algebra. A frame for R is a p-torsion free, p-adically complete and separated O_L-algebra 𝓡 with an isomorphism 𝓡/p𝓡 ≅ R and a lift σ of the Frobenius to 𝓡 (a special case of Zink's definition, footnote 9). If θ: R → R' is a map of F̄_p-algebras, a frame for θ is a morphism of O_L-algebras θ̃: 𝓡 → 𝓡' from a frame of R to a frame of R' which lifts θ and is compatible with σ. There is a unique σ-equivariant map 𝓡 → W(R). Hence every s: R → R' gives a map 𝓡 → W(R'), again denoted s. Put 𝓡_L = 𝓡 ⊗_{O_L} L.

(1.2.6): (1) S_{≼μ}(g) ⊂ Spec R is Zariski closed; (2) S_μ(g) is locally closed, and closed if μ is minuscule; (3) Spec R → π_1(G), s ↦ [μ_{G,s(g)}], is locally constant. items.name: Affine Deligne–Lusztig set and frame components
items.statement: Let b ∈ G(L). For an F̄_p-algebra R with S = Spec R and a frame 𝓡: X_{≼μ}(b)(𝓡) = {g ∈ G(𝓡_L)/G(𝓡) : S_{≼μ}(g^{-1}bσ(g)) = S}, and X_μ(b)(𝓡) is defined in the same way with S_μ. Write X_{≼μ}(b) := X_{≼μ}(b)(W(F̄_p)) (written X^G_{≼μ}(b) when G must be explicit); thus X_μ(b) = {gG(O_L) : g^{-1}bσ(g) ∈ G(O_L)p^μG(O_L)}. These sets depend only on the σ-conjugacy class of b. For g_0, g_1 ∈ X_{≼μ}(b) and R a smooth F̄_p-algebra with connected spectrum and a frame 𝓡, g_0 is connected to g_1 via R if there are g ∈ X_{≼μ}(b)(𝓡) and s_0, s_1 ∈ (Spec R)(F̄_p) with s_0(g) = g_0 and s_1(g) = g_1. ∼ is the smallest equivalence relation on X_{≼μ}(b) containing these relations, and π_0(X_{≼μ}(b)) := X_{≼μ}(b)/∼ is the set of connected components.

items.statement: Proposition (1.3.9) (setting of §§1.3.6–1.3.8; Spf R is the versal deformation space of 𝒢_x, and Spf R_G ⊂ Spf R is the G_W-adapted locus of (1.1.10)): suppose the image of x in 𝒮_K(G,X)^- has residue field k, and let Û_x be the completion of 𝒮_K(G,X)^- there. (1) Û_x may be identified with a closed subspace of Spf R containing Spf R_G. (2) Let x̃′ ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(K) be a point whose specialization x′ ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k) maps to the image of x in 𝒮_K(G,X)^-(k). Then (the images of) x̃, x̃′ lie on the same irreducible component of Û_x if and only if s_{α,0,x̃} = s_{α,0,x̃′}. (3) A deformation 𝒢 of 𝒢_x to O_K corresponds to a point of Û_x on the same irreducible component as x̃ if and only if 𝒢 is G_W-adapted. (The proof shows that this component is Spf R_G.) Corollary (1.3.11): if x, x′ ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k) have the same image in 𝒮_K(G,X)^-(k), then x = x′ if and only if s_{α,0,x} = s_{α,0,x′}.

items.statement: Lemma (1.4.6): let R be a smooth integral F̄_p-algebra with frame 𝓡, let 𝓡_n be 𝓡 viewed as an 𝓡-algebra via σ^n, and let R_n = 𝓡_n/p𝓡_n (1.4.5). Then there exist n ≥ 1, a p-divisible group 𝒢_{gx} over R_n, and a quasi-isogeny τ_g: 𝒢_{gx} → 𝒢_x ⊗ R_n over R_n, such that (1) τ_g identifies 𝔻(𝒢_{gx})(𝓡_n) with g·(𝔻(𝒢_x) ⊗_{O_L} 𝓡_n), with g viewed in G(𝓡_{n,L}) (i.e. as σ^n(g) once 𝓡_n is identified with 𝓡); (2) there is a cocharacter μ′ of gGg^{-1}, defined over 𝓡_n and conjugate to μ, such that the filtration on 𝔻(𝒢_{gx})(R_n) is induced by μ′^{-1}.

items.name: All ADLV components satisfy the Hodge condition
items.statement: Let X_υ(b)° ⊂ X_υ(b) be the maximal subset on which (1.4.3) lifts to ι_x with s_{α,0,x} = s_{α,0,ι_x(g)}; the lift is unique by (1.3.11). (a) X_υ(b)° is a union of connected components of X_υ(b) in the sense of (1.2.9), by (1.2.8), (1.4.6) and (1.4.9). (b) For a G_W-adapted lifting 𝒢̃_x of 𝒢_x to O_K (K/L finite), which gives x̃ ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(K) by (1.3.9), the map G(Q_p)/G(Z_p) → X_υ(b), g ↦ g_0, of (1.2.16)–(1.2.18) has image in X_υ(b)°. (c) By (1.2.23), 𝒢̃_x can be chosen so that G(Q_p)/G(Z_p) → π_0(X_υ(b)) is surjective. Hence X_υ(b)° = X_υ(b).
proofSteps: Use the formal tensor criterion to propagate along frame families and the component-surjective adapted lift. A p-lattice-changing quasi-isogeny is not assumed prime-to-p.

items.statement: (1.4.11)–Corollary (1.4.12): fix L̄ ↪ C. Let x ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(F̄_p), let x̃ ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(O_L̄) lift x, and let (h,1,g^p_x̃) ∈ X × G(Q_p) × G(A^p_f) map to x̃ ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C) ([Ki 2, 2.2.6]). The attached H_1(𝒜(C),Z_(p)) ≅ V_{Z(p)} gives V_{Z_p} ≅ T_p𝒢_x̃ taking s_α to s_{α,p,x̃}, and (1.2.16) then gives g_p ↦ g_{p,0}: G(Q_p)/G(Z_p) → X_υ(b). items.name: Fixed-field and geometric tensor automorphism groups
items.statement: Setting of §2.1: k ⊂ F̄_p is a finite extension of k_E, r = [k:F_p] (not [k_E:F_p]), q = p^r, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k), and x̄ is the induced F̄_p-point. (2.1.1) For l ≠ p, the Frobenius-invariant s_{α,l,x} ∈ H¹_ét(𝒜_x̄,Q_l)^⊗ define G_l ⊂ GL(H¹_ét(𝒜_x̄,Q_l)), identified with G_{Q_l} canonically up to conjugation by the image of K^p → G(Q_l). (2.1.2) γ_l ∈ G(Q_l) is the geometric q-Frobenius; I_{l/k} is the centralizer of γ_l in G_{Q_l}; I_l = I_{l,n} is the centralizer of γ_l^n for n sufficiently divisible, which stabilizes because the Zariski closures of ⟨γ_l^n⟩ do. Fix 𝔻(𝒢_x) ≅ V*_{Z(p)} ⊗ W taking s_{α,0,x} to s_α. Then Frobenius on 𝔻(𝒢_x) is δσ with δ ∈ G(K_0), well defined up to σ-conjugacy by G(W), and γ_p = δσ(δ)⋯σ^{r-1}(δ). Define I_{p/k}(R) = {α ∈ G(W ⊗_{Z_p} R) : δσ(α) = αδ} ⊂ J_δ, so γ_p ∈ I_{p/k}(Q_p) and I_{p/k} ⊗ K_0 ≅ Z_{G_{K_0}}(γ_p) [Ko 6, Lem. 5.4]; define I_{p,n} the same way with W(k_n), and I_p = I_{p,n} for n sufficiently divisible. Aut_Q(𝒜_x)(R) = (End_Q(𝒜_x) ⊗ R)^×. I_{/k} ⊂ Aut_Q(𝒜_x) is the subgroup fixing the s_{α,l,x} (all l ≠ p) and the s_{α,0,x}, and γ ∈ I_{/k}(Q) is the q-Frobenius. I ⊂ Aut_Q(𝒜_x ⊗_k F̄_p) is the subgroup fixing s_{α,0,x} and all s_{α,l,x}. There are natural maps I_{/k} → I_{l/k} (γ ↦ γ_l) and I → I_l, and I → I_p is i ↦ 𝔻(i^{-1}).

items.name: Continuous cohomology of a crossed module
items.statement: Let H̃ → H be a crossed module and Δ a profinite group acting on it: compatible actions on H̃ and H, continuous for the discrete topology, with τ(h̃^h) = τ(h̃)^{τ(h)}. For i = −1, 0, 1 there are pointed sets H^i(Δ, H̃→H) [Bo, §3] such that (1) H^i(Δ, 1→H) = H^i(Δ, H) for i = 0, 1; (2) they are invariant under quasi-isomorphism (item H03); (3) there is a long exact sequence (item H04); (4) if the cokernel of H̃ → H is abelian, H^i(Δ, H̃→H) has a canonical abelian group structure (but see the sourceIssue on (3.2.7)(4)). By (1) and (2), if H̃ ⊂ H then H^i(Δ, H̃→H) = H^i(Δ, H/H̃) for i = 0, 1. For a crossed module 𝓗̃ → 𝓗 of algebraic groups over k, write H^i(k, 𝓗̃→𝓗) := H^i(Gal(k̄/k), 𝓗̃(k̄) → 𝓗(k̄)); when 𝓗̃ = 1, write H^i(k,𝓗) and Z^i(k,𝓗).

items.name: Serre condition on a torus cocharacter
items.statement: Let T be a Q-torus and ι the complex conjugation. η ∈ X_*(T) satisfies the Serre condition if (τ−1)(ι+1)(η) = (ι+1)(τ−1)(η) = 0 for all τ ∈ Gal(Q̄/Q). T satisfies the Serre condition if every η ∈ X_*(T) does. This is equivalent to T being isogenous to T_1^+ × T_1^−, where T_1^+ is Q-split and T_1^−(R) is compact. Any such torus splits over a CM field.

items.statement: (3.6.1) Let φ: 𝔔 → 𝔊_{G/G̃} be a morphism (G̃ the simply connected cover of G^der, ρ: G̃ → G). X̃^p(φ) is the set of families (g_l, ε_l)_{l≠p,∞} with (g_l) ∈ G(Ā^p_f) (Ā^p_f the restricted product of the Q̄_l) and ε_l ∈ Z^1(Q_l, G̃(Q̄_l)) a cocycle for the twisted action τ(h) = g_lτ(g_l)^{-1}τ(h)τ(g_l)g_l^{-1}, such that ε_l(τ)·Int(g_l)∘ξ_l(τ) = φ(l)∘ζ_l(τ) in G(Q̄_l) (so ε_l is an isomorphism Int(g_l)∘ξ_l ≅ φ(l)∘ζ_l, ξ_l: 𝔊_l → 𝔊_G(l) → 𝔊_{G/G̃}(l)), and (ε_l(τ_l))_l ∈ G̃(Ā^p_f) for every (τ_l) ∈ ∏_l Gal(Q̄_l/Q_l). G̃(Ā^p_f) acts by h·(g_l,ε_l) = (h_lg_l, τ ↦ ε_l·τ(h_l)h_l^{-1}) (twisted τ), and X^p(φ) := G̃(Ā^p_f)\X̃^p(φ). X_p(φ) is the set of g ∈ G(Q̄_p)/(G̃(Q_p^ur)·G_{Z_p}(Z_p^ur)) such that θ_g = Int(g^{-1})∘φ(p)∘ζ_p is induced by a morphism θ^ur_g: 𝔇 → 𝔊^ur_{G/G̃}(p) := 𝔊^ur_G/G̃(Q_p^ur) (on the nose: θ_g(1⋊τ) = 1⋊τ for τ ∈ Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^ur); footnote 19: not stable under isomorphism) with θ^ur_g(d_σ) = b_g⋊σ and κ̃_G(b_g) = [−µ] ∈ π_1(G) (not π_1(G)_Γ). X(φ) := X_p(φ) × X^p(φ); it depends on φ itself, an isomorphism φ ≅ φ′ giving an identification X(φ) ≅ X(φ′) canonical only up to Aut(φ). If G^der = G̃, (g_l,ε_l) ↦ (image of g_l) is a bijection X^p(φ) ≅ X^{p′}(φ) := {g ∈ G^ab(Ā^p_f): Int(g_l)∘ξ_l = φ(l)∘ζ_l ∀l}. (3) For g_0 ∈ π̃(G,φ_0), g ↦ g_0·g is a bijection π(G) := G(Q)^-_+\G(A_f)/G_{Z_p}(Z_p) ≅ π(G,φ_0) := lim_{K^p} π̃(G,φ_0)/G(Q̄)^♮_+·K^p (K^p compact open in G(A^p_f)); so π(G,φ_0) is a π(G)-torsor. Here H^- is closure in G(A_f), G̃(A_f) means its image, and G(Q)_+ = G(Q) ∩ G(Q̄)^♮_+ = G(Q) ∩ (preimage of G^ad(R)^+) (Deligne's convention; not G(Q) ∩ G(R)^0). If φ, φ′: 𝔔 → 𝔊_G are admissible and φ^ad, φ′^ad are conjugate by g^ad ∈ G^ad(Q̄), then π(G,φ) and π(G,φ′) are canonically isomorphic π(G)-torsors: left multiplication by a lift g̃ ∈ G̃(Q̄) of g^ad ((g_l,ε_l) ↦ (g̃g_l, g̃ε_lg̃^{-1}), g_p ↦ g̃g_p) followed by the identification of π(G, g̃φg̃^{-1}) and π(G,φ′) via (3.6.2)(3); the result does not depend on g̃. (3.6.5): these identifications define π(G,φ_0) for all φ with φ^ad conjugate to φ_0. If G^der = G̃ and φ_ab~ = φ′_ab~, the underlying sets of π(G,φ) and π(G,φ′) coincide, but the (3.6.4) identification is in general not the identity (for G^der ≠ G̃ an analogous 'tautological' identification exists but is not used).

X_p(ψ_{µ_T}) = {t ∈ T(Q̄_p)/𝒯°(Z_p^ur): θ_t = Int(t^{-1})∘ψ_{µ_T}(p)∘ζ_p is induced by θ^ur_t: 𝔇 → 𝔊^ur_T with θ^ur_t(d_σ) = b_t⋊σ and κ̃_T(b_t) = [−µ_T] ∈ X_*(T)_I}. X(ψ_{µ_T}) = X_p × X^p and S(ψ_{µ_T}) = T(Q)^-\X(ψ_{µ_T}) (closure in T(A_f)). For a protorus T = lim T_i: X(ψ_{µ_T}) = lim X(ψ_{µ_{T_i}}), S(ψ_{µ_T}) = lim S(ψ_{µ_{T_i}}).

There is a unique system, indexed by the objects of SH_p(G^ad,X^ad), of isomorphisms of π(G)-torsors ϑ_G: π(G,φ_0) ≅ π(G,X) = π_0(𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C)) such that (1) ϑ is functorial for morphisms in SH_p(G^ad,X^ad); (2) for every triple (T, h_T, i) (T a Q-torus, h_T: S → T_R, µ_T = µ_{h_T}, i: T → G over Q with i∘h_T ∈ X) such that (i∘ψ_{µ_T})^ad is conjugate to φ_0, the square S(ψ_{µ_T}) → T(Q)^-\T(A_f)/𝒯°(Z_p) (3.6.7) → π(G,X) (3.6.9) equals S(ψ_{µ_T}) → π(G, i∘ψ_{µ_T}) = π(G,φ_0) → π(G,X) via ϑ_G.

items.name: Twisted adelic level structure
items.statement: Let A/S be an abelian scheme with an action of Z, and V a Q-vector space of dimension 2dim_S A with a faithful Z-action. Let C_Z ⊂ GL(V) be the commutant of Z. Case S a Q-scheme: let V̂(A) = lim_n A[n], V̂(A)_Q = V̂(A) ⊗ Q, K ⊂ C_Z(A_f) compact (not necessarily open), and ε_K ∈ Γ(S, Isom_Z(V_{A_f}, V̂(A)_Q)/K). Let P be a Z-torsor. Its induced GL(V)-torsor is trivial, so identify P with the fibre of GL(V) → GL(V)/Z over some ω ∈ (GL(V)/Z)(Q), and choose a lift ω̃ ∈ GL(V)(F), F/Q finite Galois. Then (4.1.3) identifies V^P with ω̃^{-1}V ⊂ V ⊗_Q F, and by (4.1.4) the isomorphism ω̃^{-1}: V ≅ V^P depends only on ω. Set K^ω = ωKω^{-1}. Define ε^ω_{K^ω} ∈ Γ(S, Isom_Z(V_{A_f}, V̂(A^P)_Q)/K^ω) étale locally by V_{A_f} → V^P_{A_f} → V̂(A)^P_Q ≅ V̂(A^P)_Q (first map ω̃^{-1}, second ε_K^P). Case S a Z_(p)-scheme: do the same with K^p ⊂ C_Z(A_f^p) and ε_{K^p} ∈ Γ(S, Isom_Z(V_{A_f^p}, V̂^p(A)_Q)/K^p); this gives ε^ω_{K^{pω}}. (For the Z-equivariance of ε^ω, Z must act on V_{A_f} through z ↦ ωzω^{-1}; see sourceIssues.)

items.name: Kottwitz triple at a finite level
items.statement: Let r ≥ 1, k = F_{p^r}, K_0 = Frac W(k). A Kottwitz triple of level r is k = (γ0, (γ_l)_{l≠p}, δ) with: γ0 ∈ G(Q) up to G(Q̄)-conjugacy; (γ_l)_{l≠p} ∈ G(A_f^p); δ ∈ G(K_0) up to σ-conjugacy by G(W(k)). The conditions are: (i) γ0 is conjugate to (γ_l)_{l≠p} in G(Ā_f^p), where Ā_f^p is the restricted product Π'_{l≠p} Q̄_l (3.3.6); (ii) γ0 is conjugate to γ_p = δσ(δ)…σ^{r−1}(δ) in G(Q̄_p); (iii) the image of γ0 in G(R) is elliptic; (iv) the global inner-form condition (K02). (γ0^m, (γ_l^m), δ) is a triple of level rm. Impose the smallest equivalence relation identifying each triple with these; an equivalence class is called a Kottwitz triple.

items.name: Stabilizer arithmetic group of a refined triple
items.statement: Let G^ad(Z_(p))^I be the kernel of the composite G^ad(Z_(p)) → H^1(Q, Z_G) → H^1(Q, I), and G^ad(Z_(p))^{+,I} = G^ad(Z_(p))^I ∩ G^ad(Z_(p))^+. Put A(G_{Z(p)})^I = G(A_f^p) *_{G(Z(p))_+} G^ad(Z_(p))^{+,I}. Let G(Z̄_(p))^{♮,I}_+ be the preimage of G^ad(Z_(p))^{+,I} in G(Q̄). For h in this preimage, the cocycle τ ↦ τ(h)h^{-1} ∈ Z^1(Q,Z_G) becomes trivial in H^1(Q,I). So there is i_h ∈ I(Q̄) with h^{-1}τ(h) = i_h^{-1}τ(i_h) for all τ ∈ Gal(Q̄/Q), where τ(i_h) uses the Q-structure of I. Via ι, i_h is regarded as an element of G(Ā_f^p) and of G(Q̄_p).

items.name: Special Kottwitz triple from a toric datum
items.statement: Let T be a Q-torus, h_T: S → T_R and i: T ↪ G with i∘h_T ∈ X. Then T/(Z_G ∩ T) satisfies the Serre condition, and since Z_G^0 does, so does T. By (3.5.7) ψ_{μ_{h_T}} factors through P, giving ψ_{μ_{h_T}}: P → G_T. Let L/Q be a finite CM Galois extension over which μ_{h_T} is defined, and δ_n ∈ P^L(Q) as in (3.5.4). Then ν(p)^L_n = −ν_{δ_n}. After increasing n there is c ∈ P^L(Q̂_p^ur), which can be chosen independently of n, with cν(p)^L_n(p^{-1})σ^n(c)^{-1} = δ_n. With t ∈ T(Q̄_p) as in (3.6.6) (it exists by (3.6.7)), θ_t^ur induces 𝔓^L(p)^ur → 𝔊_T^ur; after increasing n this is a morphism of Q_{p^n}/Q_p-gerbs. Set γ0 = ψ^Δ_{μ_{h_T}}(δ_n) and define δ ∈ T(Q_{p^n}) by θ_t^ur(c d_σ c^{-1}) = δ ⋊ σ. Then δσ(δ)…σ^{n−1}(δ) = γ0, and δ is well defined up to σ-conjugacy in T(Q_p^ur). Put k(T,h_T) = (γ0, (γ_l = γ0)_{l≠p}, δ). Then i_*(k(T,h_T)) is a Kottwitz triple: (i)–(iii) hold, and (iv) holds with I = I_φ, φ = i∘ψ_{μ_{h_T}} admissible by (3.5.8). A Kottwitz triple k is called special if k ~ i_*(k(T,h_T)) for some such (T, h_T, i).

items.name: Triple attached to an admissible morphism
items.statement: Setting of §4.3 (Z_G^0 satisfies the Serre condition; G has a reductive model over Z_p). Let φ: Q → G_G be admissible (it factors through P by (3.5.7)) and g = (g_0, g^p) ∈ X_p(φ) × X^p(φ). Choose a CM field L with φ factoring through P^L and n with [L_p:Q_p] | n. Set (γ_l)_{l≠p} = (g^p)^{-1} φ^Δ(δ_n) g^p ∈ G(A_f^p). With φ(p)_{g_0} = g_0^{-1}φ(p)g_0, which is induced by θ^ur_{g_0}: P^L(p)^ur → G^ur_G (for n large, by a map of Q_{p^n}/Q_p-gerbs), take c ∈ P^L(Q̂_p^ur) as in (4.3.9) and c' ∈ P^L(Q_{p^n}) so close to c that θ^ur_{g_0}(c'c^{-1}) ∈ G(Ẑ_p^ur), and define δ ∈ G(Q_{p^n}) by θ^ur_{g_0}(c'^{-1} c d_σ c^{-1} c') = δ ⋊ σ. δ is well defined up to σ-conjugacy by G(Z_{p^n}), and up to σ-conjugacy by G(Ẑ_p^ur) it equals δ' with δ' ⋊ σ = θ^ur_{g_0}(d_σ). By [LR, Lem. 5.4], for n suitably divisible and large, φ(δ_n) is G(Q̄)-conjugate to some γ_0 ∈ G(Q), and γ_0 is elliptic in G(R). Then k(g) = (γ_0, (γ_l)_{l≠p}, δ) is a Kottwitz triple satisfying (4.3.1)(iv) with I = I_φ, via I_{γ_0} ⊗ Q̄ ≅ I_{φ'} ⊗ Q̄ ≅ I_φ ⊗ Q̄. It depends only on the image of g in S(φ) = I_φ(Q)\X(φ), and its equivalence class k(φ) depends only on φ.

The bijection is equivariant for geometric Φ_r2, ZG2(Qp) and A(G2); tau∈I_phi^ad(Af) depends only on the adjoint class φ0.
proofSteps: Take the connected fiber in the Hodge-type comparison, induce along A(G2) using the integral central derived isogeny and common reflex Frobenius, then decompose lift conjugacy classes.

items.name: Integral crystalline tensors for a p-divisible group
items.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over O_K with G_K-invariant tensors (s_α) ⊂ T_pG^⊗ defining a reductive G ⊂ GL(T_pG), and suppose k is separably closed, or G_{Z_p} is connected and k finite. Then (1) the comparison images s_{α,0} lie in D(G)(W)^⊗; (2) there is an isomorphism T_pG*(−1) ⊗ W ≅ D(G) taking s_α to s_{α,0}; (3) the filtration on D(G)(k) is induced by a G_W-valued cocharacter.
proofSteps: Deduce from Theorem (1.1.6) and the reductivity of the stabilizer.

The proof gives more: b = h·p^{υ_0} with h ∈ G_W(W), and this stronger form is used in the proof of (1.1.13).
proofSteps: Cartan decomposition of b, then conjugate the cocharacter.

items.statement: Setting of (1.3.6): k ⊂ F̄_p a subfield containing k_E, W = W(k), K ⊂ L̄ a finite totally ramified extension of W[1/p], x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k), x̃ ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K) specializing to x, and s_{α,p,x̃} ∈ H¹_ét(𝒜_{x̃,K̄},Z_p)^⊗ (Gal(K̄/K)-invariant). Then (1) under the p-adic comparison isomorphism H¹_ét(𝒜_{x̃,K̄},Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_cris ≅ H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W) ⊗_W B_cris the s_{α,p,x̃} map to φ-invariant tensors s_{α,0,x̃} ∈ Fil⁰(H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W)^⊗); (2) there is a W-linear isomorphism H¹_ét(𝒜_{x̃,K̄},Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} W ≅ H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W) taking s_{α,p,x̃} to s_{α,0,x̃}; in particular the s_{α,0,x̃} define a reductive group scheme G_W ⊂ GL(H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W)) isomorphic to G_{Z(p)} ⊗_{Z(p)} W; (3) the filtration on H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W) ⊗_W k is given by μ_0^{-1}, where μ_0 is a G_W-valued cocharacter conjugate to μ_h for h ∈ X.
proofSteps: Apply Corollary (1.1.7) to the p-divisible group of A_x̃; compare μ_0 with μ_h.
