items.name: The tensor space M^⊗ and the crystalline tensors s̃_α, s_{α,0}
items.statement: For a ring R and a finite free R-module M, M^⊗ is the direct sum of the R-modules obtained from M by taking duals, tensor products, symmetric and exterior powers. The stabiliser of a collection (s_α) ⊂ M^⊗ is a closed subgroup scheme of GL(M). For L ∈ Rep^{cris°}_{G_K} with G_K-invariant (s_α) ⊂ L^⊗ defining G_{Z_p} ⊂ GL(L), regard s_α as morphisms 1 → L^⊗ and apply 𝔐 of (1.1.2) to get s̃_α ∈ 𝔐(L)^⊗. Then s_{α,0} := s̃_α|_{u=0} ∈ (𝔐/u𝔐)^⊗ ⊂ D_cris(L ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p)^⊗ is the image of s_α under the p-adic comparison isomorphism (by functoriality of (1.1.2)(1)).
items.note: Used in (1.1.4) and (1.1.7) and throughout. Symmetric and exterior powers are included because the proof of [Ki 2, 1.3.2] uses them (footnote 7). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Flat subgroups with reductive generic fibre are tensor stabilisers
items.statement: Let R be a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring, M a finite free R-module and G ⊂ GL(M) a closed R-flat subgroup with reductive generic fibre. Then G is the pointwise stabiliser of a collection of elements of M^⊗.
items.note: Cited black box. Used implicitly whenever tensors are 'extended' to cut out a smaller subgroup: t_β for G' and t_γ for G'' in (1.2.19), t_{β,0} for the Levi M in (1.2.23), and the Hodge tensors in (1.3.6). The footnote adds that Deligne has an argument using only duals and tensor products. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The filtered φ-module ℳ(𝔐) over S
items.statement: For a p-divisible group 𝒢 over a scheme on which p is locally nilpotent, D(𝒢) denotes its contravariant Dieudonné F-crystal with Frobenius φ, 𝒢* its Cartier dual and T_p𝒢 its Tate module. For 𝔐 ∈ BT^φ_{/𝔖}, set ℳ(𝔐) = S ⊗_𝔖 φ*(𝔐) with the induced Frobenius and Fil^1 ℳ(𝔐) = {x ∈ S ⊗_{φ,𝔖} 𝔐 : (1⊗φ)(x) ∈ Fil^1 S ⊗_𝔖 𝔐 ⊂ S ⊗_𝔖 𝔐}. Then Fil^1 ℳ(𝔐) = S·Fil^1(φ*(𝔐)) + Fil^1 S·ℳ(𝔐).
items.note: Target of the comparison D(𝒢)(S) ≅ ℳ(𝔐(𝒢)) in (1.1.6). Used in the proof of (1.1.13). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Rational identification of the crystals of 𝒢 and a deformation
items.statement: Let 𝒢̃ be a deformation to O_K of a p-divisible group 𝒢 over k. There is a unique φ-invariant isomorphism D(𝒢)(W) ⊗_W S[1/p] ≅ D(𝒢̃)(S) ⊗_S S[1/p] lifting the identity on D(𝒢)(W) ⊗_W K_0. If 𝒢̃ is G_W-adapted, this isomorphism sends s_{α,0} to s̃_α, so the subgroup of GL(D(𝒢̃)(S)[1/p]) defined by the s̃_α is identified with G_W ⊗_W S[1/p].
items.note: Cited black box. It is the identification used in the proof of Lemma (1.1.9) ('we are identifying the subgroup … with G_W ⊗_W K'). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Filtration of an adapted deformation (Lemma 1.1.9)
items.statement: In the setting of (1.1.8), let 𝒢̃ be a G_W-adapted deformation of 𝒢. Then the filtration on D(𝒢̃)(O_K) ⊗_{O_K} K is induced by a G_W ⊗_W K-valued cocharacter, and any such cocharacter is conjugate to μ_0^{-1}.
items.note: Numbered lemma with no item. The extraction's D08 wrongly put its conclusion into the definition of adaptedness. The proof uses [Ki 2, 1.4.5], [Ki 2, 1.1.4], [Ki 2, 1.1.5], [DG, XXVI 1.8] (Levi subgroups of a parabolic are conjugate under its unipotent radical) and [DG, IX 3.3] (rigidity of conjugacy of cocharacters). Used in (1.1.19), (1.2.18) and (1.3.7). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Z_p-structure U, the group G_{Z_p} and the Frobenius element b
items.statement: Let 𝒢 and (s_{α,0}) ⊂ D(𝒢)(W)^⊗ be as in (1.1.8), but without assuming that the filtration on D(𝒢)(k) is given by a G_W-valued cocharacter. Suppose U is a finite free Z_p-module with an isomorphism U ⊗_{Z_p} W ≅ D(𝒢)(W) under which s_{α,0} ∈ U^⊗. The s_{α,0} then define a reductive Z_p-subgroup G = G_{Z_p} ⊂ GL(U) with G_{Z_p} ⊗_{Z_p} W ≅ G_W. For R → R' and X an R-module or R-scheme, X_{R'} := X ⊗_R R', and G_R := G ⊗_{Z_p} R. Since the s_{α,0} ∈ U^⊗ are φ-invariant, φ on D(𝒢)(W) ⊗_W W[1/p] has the form bσ with b ∈ G(W[1/p]). For a cocharacter μ, p^μ := μ(p).
items.note: These are 'the above assumptions' of (1.1.12), (1.1.13) and (1.1.19). Specialised to k = F̄_p in (1.2.15). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Isogeny category and quasi-isogeny
items.statement: For a Z-linear category C, C ⊗_Z Q is the category with the same objects and Hom groups tensored with Q (the isogeny category of C). An isomorphism in C ⊗_Z Q is a quasi-isogeny. This is applied to p-divisible groups over a base and to Dieudonné modules of p-divisible groups. From here on, D(𝒢) denotes D(𝒢)(W).
items.note: Used in (1.1.19), (1.2.16) and (1.4.2). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: p-divisible groups realising an admissible filtration
items.statement: Let K/K_0 be finite totally ramified and p > 2. In the situation of (1.1.19) (μ^{-1} inducing an admissible filtration on D(𝒢)_K), there is a p-divisible group 𝒢̃' over O_K and an isomorphism of weakly admissible filtered φ-modules D(𝒢')_{K_0} ≅ D(𝒢)_{K_0}, 𝒢' = 𝒢̃' ⊗ k. On the left the filtration (after ⊗K) is that of 𝒢̃'; on the right it is induced by μ^{-1}. This isomorphism induces a quasi-isogeny θ: 𝒢 → 𝒢'.
items.locator: proof of Proposition (1.1.19), p. 11 (cited: [Ki 1, 2.2.6]; cf. [Br, Thm. 1.4])
items.note: Cited black box: every crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in {0,1} comes from a p-divisible group over O_K. It also uses Dieudonné theory over the perfect field k (supplier P08) to pass from rational Dieudonné modules to a quasi-isogeny. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Triviality of the torsor of tensor-preserving isomorphisms
items.statement: Let V = T_p𝒢̃ ⊗ Q_p and V' = T_p𝒢̃' ⊗ Q_p be as in the proof of (1.1.19), with G_K-invariant tensors s_α, s'_α corresponding to s_{α,0}. The scheme of Q_p-linear isomorphisms V' → V taking s'_α to s_α is a G_{Q_p}-torsor. It is trivial when the filtrations on D(𝒢)_K given by 𝒢̃ and 𝒢̃' are induced by conjugate G-valued cocharacters.
items.locator: proof of Proposition (1.1.19), p. 11 (cited: [Wi, Cor. 4.5.3] together with Colmez–Fontaine, weakly admissible implies admissible)
items.note: Cited black box. It yields the Q_p-linear isomorphism (1.1.20). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Relative-position loci S_μ(g), S_{≼μ}(g)
items.statement: Let 𝓡 be a frame for an F̄_p-algebra R, g ∈ G(𝓡_L) and μ ∈ X_*(T) dominant. S_μ(g) = {s ∈ Spec R : s(g) ∈ G(W(κ̄(s))) p^μ G(W(κ̄(s)))}, where κ̄(s) is an algebraic closure of κ(s) and s(g) is formed via 𝓡 → W(κ̄(s)). S_{≼μ}(g) = ⋃_{μ' ≼ μ} S_{μ'}(g), the union over dominant μ' ≼ μ. For s ∈ S_μ(g) with μ dominant, write μ_{s(g)} = μ.
items.note: Needed to state (1.2.6), (1.2.8) and (1.2.9). The paper says 'dominant characters'; cocharacters are meant. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Étale coverings and canonical frames
items.statement: An étale covering is a faithfully flat étale morphism R → R'. If 𝓡 is a frame for R, then any étale morphism R → R' admits a canonical frame 𝓡 → 𝓡'.
items.note: Cited black box. Needed to state Lemma (1.2.8) and used in §1.4 (proof of (1.4.4)). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: σ-conjugate with dominant Newton point lying in its centraliser
items.statement: Every b ∈ G(L) is σ-conjugate to some b' with ν_{b'} ∈ X_*(T) ⊗_Z Q dominant (hence σ-invariant) and b' ∈ M_{b'}.
items.note: Cited black box. It enters the definition of HN-indecomposability and the proof of (1.2.23). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Hodge–Newton reduction of ADLVs to a standard Levi
items.statement: Let b' be as in [CKV, Lem. 2.5.2] and M ⊃ M_{b'} a standard Levi subgroup with κ_M(b') = μ^{♮,M} in π_1(M)_Γ. Then the natural map X^M_μ(b') → X^G_μ(b') = X_μ(b) is a bijection and induces a bijection on connected components.
items.note: Cited black box. Essential in the proof of (1.2.23) (pp. 17–18). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Fibres of π_0(X_υ(b)) → π_0(X_{υ^ad}(b^ad))
items.statement: In the setting of (1.2.21), the non-empty fibres of π_0(X_υ(b)) → π_0(X_{υ^ad}(b^ad)) are X_*(Z_G)^Γ-torsors, λ ∈ X_*(Z_G)^Γ acting through the central element p^λ ∈ Z_G(Q_p).
items.note: Cited black box. It gives h = g_0 z with z ∈ Z_G(Q_p) in the last step of (1.2.21). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Setting of (1.2.15): U, G_{Z_p}, b, μ_0, υ_0 over F̄_p
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a p-divisible group over F̄_p, D(𝒢) := D(𝒢)(O_L), and (s_{α,0}) ⊂ D(𝒢)^⊗ φ-invariant tensors defining a reductive subgroup G_{O_L} ⊂ GL(D(𝒢)) (printed '⊂ D(𝒢)^⊗'). Suppose U is a finite free Z_p-module with U ⊗_{Z_p} O_L ≅ D(𝒢) and s_{α,0} ∈ U^⊗. The s_{α,0} then define a reductive G = G_{Z_p} ⊂ GL(U). For another such U', the isomorphisms U → U' respecting the s_{α,0} form a G_{Z_p}-torsor, which is trivial (this needs G_{Z_p} connected). φ = bσ with b ∈ G(L), independent of U up to σ-conjugation by G_{O_L}(O_L). By (1.1.12) the filtration on D(𝒢)(F̄_p) is induced by a G_{O_L}-valued μ_0^{-1} and b ∈ G(O_L)p^{υ_0}G(O_L) with υ_0 = σ(μ_0^{-1}). Hence 1 ∈ X_{υ_0}(b), and c_{b,μ} may be taken to be the neutral element of π_1(G) (printed 'c_{b,μ} = 1').
items.note: Standing setting for (1.2.16)–(1.2.23) and, through (1.3.7), for §1.4. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: The map g ↦ g_0 from Tate-lattice changes to Dieudonné-lattice changes
items.statement: Let K/L be finite, K̄ an algebraic closure of K, and 𝒢̃ a G_{O_L}-adapted lifting of 𝒢 to a p-divisible group over O_K. By (1.1.13) take U = T_p𝒢̃*(−1) with the tensors s_α, and fix an isomorphism (1.2.17) T_p𝒢̃*(−1) ⊗_{Z_p} O_L ≅ D(𝒢) taking s_α to s_{α,0}. For g ∈ G(Q_p) there is a finite K'/K in K̄ such that the lattice g^{-1}·T_p𝒢̃ is G_{K'}-stable, hence is the Tate module of a p-divisible group 𝒢̃' over O_{K'} (printed 'over K''). With 𝒢' = 𝒢̃' ⊗ F̄_p, the quasi-isogeny θ: 𝒢 → 𝒢' identifies D(𝒢') with g_0·D(𝒢) for some g_0 ∈ GL(D(𝒢) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p). By Lemma (1.2.18), g_0 ∈ G(L).
items.note: This is the construction behind D15, D16, X10 and X11. For the convention on how G(Q_p) acts on T_p𝒢̃ (needed for well-definedness on G(Q_p)/G(Z_p) and for κ̃(g_0) = κ̃(g)), see notes. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: HN-indecomposability passes to the adjoint group
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Z_p, b ∈ G(L) and υ minuscule with X_υ(b) ≠ ∅. If (υ, b) is HN-indecomposable for G, then (υ^ad, b^ad) is HN-indecomposable for G^ad. The key fact: for every standard Levi M ⊃ T, the map π_1(M)_Γ → π_1(G)_Γ ⊕ π_1(M/Z_G)_Γ is injective.
items.locator: proof of Proposition (1.2.21), first paragraph, p. 17
items.note: Unnumbered claim needed to apply (1.2.14) to the simple factors of G^ad. The printed justification is imprecise (see the new gap entry). A correct proof: by (1.2.3) for G and for G^ad, both connecting maps into (Q^∨/Q^∨_M)_Γ vanish, so ker(π_1(M)_Γ → π_1(G)_Γ) ≅ (Q^∨/Q^∨_M)_Γ ≅ ker(π_1(M/Z_G)_Γ → π_1(G^ad)_Γ) compatibly. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Hodge cocharacter μ_h, weight w_h, reflex field and Sh_K
items.statement: (1.3.1) For a Shimura datum (G,X) [De 2, §2.1] and h ∈ X, μ_h is the cocharacter of G_C given on R-points by R^× → (R × c^*(R))^× = (R ⊗_R C)^× = S(R) →^h G_C(R), and w_h = μ_h^{-1}μ_h^{c-1}. For K = K_pK^p ⊂ G(A_f) with K^p sufficiently small, Sh_K(G,X)_C = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K is an algebraic variety (Baily–Borel) with a model Sh_K(G,X) over E = E(G,X), the field of definition of the conjugacy class of μ_h [Mi 3, II §4,5], and Sh_{K_p}(G,X) = lim_{K^p} Sh_K(G,X).
items.note: μ_h fixes μ (1.4.1) and the Hodge filtration convention (1.3.7)(3), and w_h is used in (2.3.1)(3). P13 imports canonical models, but no item defines μ_h or w_h. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Integral Hodge embedding and choice of Siegel level ([Ki 2, 2.1.2, 2.3.1, 2.3.2])
items.statement: (1.3.3) Suppose K_p = G_{Z(p)}(Z_p) for a reductive G_{Z(p)} over Z_(p) with generic fibre G. Then ι: (G,X) ↪ (GSp,S^±) is induced by an embedding G_{Z(p)} ↪ GL(V_{Z(p)}) for some Z_(p)-lattice V_{Z(p)} ⊂ V. After Zarhin's trick (replacing V_{Z(p)} by Hom_{Z(p)}(V_{Z(p)},V_{Z(p)})^4), ψ is perfect on V_{Z(p)}. With K′_p = GSp(V_{Z(p)})(Z_p), for each K^p there is a compact open K′^p ⊂ GSp(A^p_f) containing K^p such that ι induces an embedding Sh_K(G,X) ↪ Sh_{K′}(GSp,S^±) of E-schemes, K′ = K′_pK′^p.
items.note: This is a black box from [Ki 2]. S01 builds 𝒮_K(G,X) on it but states neither the lattice V_{Z(p)} nor the choice of K′^p. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Abelian schemes up to prime-to-p isogeny, weak polarizations, K′^p-level structures
items.statement: (1.3.4) For a Z_(p)-scheme T and an abelian scheme B/T, V̂^p(B) = lim_{p∤n} B[n] (an étale local system) and V̂^p(B)_Q = V̂^p(B) ⊗ Q. Abelian schemes up to prime-to-p isogeny form the category with Hom ⊗ Z_(p), and its isomorphisms are p′-quasi-isogenies. A weak polarization of such an 𝒜 is an equivalence class of p′-quasi-isogenies λ: 𝒜 ≅ 𝒜^* some multiple of which is a polarization, with λ ~ λ′ when they differ by an element of Z_(p)^×. Isom(V_{A^p_f}, V̂^p(𝒜)_Q) is the étale sheaf of isomorphisms compatible with the pairings from ψ and λ up to an A^{p×}_f-scalar, and a K′^p-level structure is a section ε^p_{K′} ∈ Γ(T, Isom(V_{A^p_f}, V̂^p(𝒜)_Q)/K′^p). For K′^p sufficiently small, T ↦ {(𝒜,λ,ε^p_{K′})}/≅ is representable by a smooth Z_(p)-scheme 𝒮_{K′}(GSp,S^±) with generic fibre Sh_{K′}(GSp,S^±) (cf. [Ko 4, §5]).
items.note: P12 imports Siegel moduli in general. The weak-polarization (Z_(p)^×) and A^{p×}_f-scalar conventions used in (1.4.2), (1.4.15) and (2.1.3) have no item. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Formal smoothness of branches, smoothness of 𝒮_K and extension of Hecke action ([Ki 2, 2.3.5, 2.3.8])
items.statement: Theorem (1.3.5): let x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)^- be a closed point of characteristic p, and Û_x the formal completion of 𝒮_K(G,X)^- at x. Then (1) the irreducible components of Û_x are formally smooth; (2) 𝒮_K(G,X) is a smooth O_(p)-scheme, and the G(A^p_f)-action on Sh_{K_p}(G,X) extends to 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X) := lim_{K^p} 𝒮_{K^pK_p}(G,X). (Standing hypotheses: p > 2, K_p hyperspecial, K^p sufficiently small.)
items.note: Cited black box, used in (1.3.9), (1.4.9), (1.4.12) and (2.1.1). S02's locator (§§1.3.5–1.3.8, the extraction) includes this number, but its statement is about tensors only. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Promotion of the Siegel level structure to a K^p-level structure ([Ki 2, 3.4.2])
items.statement: (1.3.6) If x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(T) corresponds to (𝒜_x, λ, ε^p_{K′}), then ε^p_{K′} may be promoted to a section ε^p_K ∈ Γ(T, Isom(V_{A^p_f}, V̂^p(𝒜_x)_Q)/K^p), and ε^p_K takes s_α to (s_{α,l})_{l≠p}.
items.note: Used in (1.4.14), (2.1.1) and (2.1.5) (ε^p_{K,x}). S02 covers the realizations s_{α,B}, s_{α,dR}, s_{α,l}, s_{α,p} but not this level structure. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: p-adic comparison takes étale Hodge tensors to de Rham tensors ([Bl])
items.statement: For x̃ ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(K) (K/K_0 finite), the p-adic comparison isomorphism takes s_{α,p,x̃} to s_{α,dR,x̃}. Hence, under H¹_dR(𝒜_x̃) ≅ H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W) ⊗_W K, s_{α,dR,x̃} is taken to s_{α,0,x̃}.
items.note: Cited black box; the parallel-transport step of (1.3.9)(2) depends on it. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Crystalline tensors s_{α,0,x} of a mod p point
items.statement: (1.3.10) For x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k), the tensor s_{α,0,x̃} ∈ H¹_cris(𝒜_x/W)^⊗ = 𝔻(𝒢_x)(W)^⊗ of (1.3.7) depends only on x and not on the lift x̃ (by (1.3.9)(2)). It is denoted s_{α,0,x}.
items.note: This is the object used throughout §§1.4–2 and in (1.3.11). S02a covers s_{α,0,x̃} but not its independence of x̃. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The Frobenius of a mod p point lies in G(W)p^υG(W)
items.statement: (1.4.1) Let x ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(k), r = r_E = [k_E:F_p], and x̃ ∈ 𝒮_K(G,X)(W) a lift. There is T_p𝒢_x̃ ≅ V_{Z_p} taking s_{α,p,x̃} to s_α, identifying G_{Z_p} with the stabilizer of (s_{α,p,x̃}) canonically up to inner conjugation, and an isomorphism V*_{Z_p} ⊗ W ≅ 𝔻(𝒢_x)(W) taking s_α to s_{α,0,x}. Then φ = bσ with b ∈ G(K_0), well defined up to σ-conjugation by G(W). Let μ ∈ X_*(T) be the dominant representative (for B ⊃ T as in (1.2.1)) of the conjugacy class of μ_h; it is defined over E_p and hence fixed by σ^r. Put υ_0 = σ(μ_0^{-1}) and υ = σ(μ^{-1}). Then b ∈ G(W)p^{υ_0}G(W) = G(W)p^υG(W).
items.note: S04 uses b to define Φ_r, but no item states this double-coset membership, which makes 1 ∈ X_υ(b) and (1.4.3) meaningful. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The map (1.4.3) X_υ(b) → 𝒮_{K′}(GSp,S^±)(F̄_p)
items.statement: (1.4.2)–(1.4.3): since υ is minuscule, X_{≼υ}(b) = X_υ(b) = {g ∈ G(L)/G(O_L) : g^{-1}bσ(g) ∈ G(O_L)p^υG(O_L)}. For g ∈ X_υ(b), g·𝔻(𝒢_x) is a Dieudonné module and so corresponds to a p-divisible group 𝒢_{gx} with a quasi-isogeny 𝒢_x → 𝒢_{gx} (from g𝔻(𝒢_x) ⊗ Q ≅ 𝔻(𝒢_x) ⊗ Q), and s_{α,0,x} = g(s_{α,0,x}) ∈ 𝔻(𝒢_{gx})^⊗. Let 𝒜_{gx} be the isogenous abelian variety with the induced K′-level structure and the weak polarization λ_{gx} induced from that of 𝒜_x (G ⊂ GSp). This gives (1.4.3) X_υ(b) → 𝒮_{K′}(GSp,S^±)(F̄_p), g ↦ (𝒜_{gx}, λ_{gx}). Φ = Φ_r denotes the geometric r-Frobenius on 𝒮_{K′}(GSp,S^±)(F̄_p) and on 𝒮_K(G,X)(F̄_p), and (1.4.3) commutes with Φ (p. 24).
items.note: S05 is the lift of this map, but no item defines the map itself. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Dieudonné theory over smooth F̄_p-algebras ([deJ, 2.3.4, 4.1.1])
items.statement: Used in the proof of (1.4.6): over R_n (smooth over F̄_p, with frame 𝓡_n), a lattice in 𝔻(𝒢_x) ⊗_{O_L} 𝓡_{n,L} that is stable under Frobenius, Verschiebung and the connection ∇ = 1 ⊗ d gives a Dieudonné crystal on R_n [deJ, 2.3.4]. The crystalline Dieudonné functor is an equivalence between p-divisible groups over R_n and Dieudonné crystals [deJ, 4.1.1], so quasi-isogenies of crystals come from quasi-isogenies of p-divisible groups.
items.note: Cited black box. P08 covers only perfect residue fields and PD deformations. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: O_L̄-points are represented by (h,1,g^p) ([Ki 2, 2.2.6]; cf. [Sa, Cor. 3.5(b)])
items.statement: (1.4.11) The point attached to (h,g_p,g^p) ∈ X × G(Q_p) × G(A^p_f) is an abelian variety 𝒜 up to prime-to-p isogeny with H_1(𝒜(C),Z_(p)) ≅ g_p·V_{Z(p)} ⊂ V_Q. For a fixed L̄ ↪ C and x̃ ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(O_L̄), there is (h,1,g^p_x̃) mapping to x̃ ∈ 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C). Hence H_1(𝒜_x̃(C),Z_(p)) ≅ V_{Z(p)}, and V_{Z_p} ≅ T_p𝒢_x̃ takes s_α to s_{α,p,x̃}.
items.note: Cited black box; it underlies (1.4.12) and the Betti identifications in (2.3.1) and (2.3.5). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: σ-centralizer of δ is a form of the centralizer of its norm ([Ko 6, Lem. 5.4])
items.statement: (2.1.2) I_{p/k} ⊗_{Q_p} K_0 is canonically isomorphic to the centralizer of γ_p = δσ(δ)⋯σ^{r-1}(δ) in G_{K_0}. Likewise I_{p,n} is isomorphic, after base change to L, to the centralizer of γ_p^n in G_L.
items.note: Cited black box, used for l = p in the proof of (2.3.2) and implicitly for rk I_p = rk G in (2.2.3). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Automorphisms commuting with Frobenius are defined over k
items.statement: An element of End_Q(𝒜_x ⊗_k F̄_p) commuting with the q-Frobenius γ lies in End_Q(𝒜_x). Hence I_{/k} = Z_I(γ), and every element of I, being defined over some k_n, commutes with γ^n.
items.locator: Used in the proofs of (2.1.5) ('Hence i_0 ∈ I_{/k}(Q)'), p. 30, and (2.3.2), p. 33
items.note: This is standard and not stated in the paper. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Semisimplicity of the Frobenius endomorphism
items.statement: The q-Frobenius γ is a semisimple element of End_Q(𝒜_x) (Tate). Hence γ_l and γ_p are semisimple, the identity component of the Zariski closure of ⟨γ_l⟩ is a torus, I_l and I_p ⊗ L are Levi subgroups of full rank, and γ lies in a maximal Q-torus of I.
items.note: The paper does not state this; rk I_p = rk G in (2.2.3) and 'γ ∈ T(Q)' in (2.3.1) depend on it. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Cocompact subgroups contain a minimal parabolic ([BT, Prop. 9.3])
items.statement: If H is a connected reductive group over Q_l and H′ ⊂ H is a closed subgroup with H′(Q_l)\H(Q_l) compact, then H′ contains a minimal parabolic Q_l-subgroup of H (a Borel subgroup when H is split). Hence H/H′ is proper.
items.note: Cited black box. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: I is reductive (Rosati positivity), so I_l/I_{Q_l} is affine
items.statement: I contains the scalars G_m ⊂ Aut_Q(𝒜_x), and (I/G_m)(R) is compact by positivity of the Rosati involution. Hence I is reductive, and I_l/I_{Q_l} is affine (quotient of a reductive group by a reductive subgroup).
items.locator: Proof of Corollary (2.1.7), p. 31; reused in (2.3.1)(3), p. 33
items.note: This step relies on two black boxes, Rosati positivity and Matsushima's affineness criterion. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Galois average ε̄^G, ε̄^T of a cocharacter
items.statement: (2.2.1) If ε: G_m → G is defined over a finite extension of Q_p and commutes with all its Galois conjugates, then ε̄ = ε̄^G is the fractional G-valued cocharacter [De 2, 1.3.4] obtained by averaging the Galois conjugates of ε. If ε factors through a torus T ⊂ G defined over Q_p, then ε̄ may be viewed as ε̄^T ∈ X_*(T)_Q = X_*(T) ⊗ Q. Also, ν_δ is central in J_δ and hence in I_p ⊂ J_δ.
items.note: B02 defines μ̄ for the conjugacy class only. The torus version, relative to T's own Q_p-structure, is what (2.2.2) and (2.2.5) use. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Rational dominant representative of a Galois-stable class ([Ko 1, 1.1.3(a)])
items.statement: If G is quasi-split over a field F with a Borel B over F, then a G(F̄)-conjugacy class of cocharacters stable under Gal(F̄/F) contains a unique B-dominant member, and that member is defined over F.
items.note: Cited black box; also implicit in (1.4.1) ('μ is defined over E_p'). Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Iwasawa decomposition
items.statement: For G reductive over Z_p and a parabolic P = MN of G_{Q_p}, G(L) = N(L)M(L)G(O_L). Moreover M(L) ∩ G(O_L) is hyperspecial in M(L), with Cartan decomposition over X_*(T_2).
items.note: Standard black box. Planned: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4 plans the Iwasawa and Cartan decompositions.

items.name: Newton point and Kottwitz point agree in π_1(M)_Q ([RR, Thm. 4.2(ii)])
items.statement: For M connected reductive over Q_p and m ∈ M(L), the images of ν_m and κ_M(m) in π_1(M)_Γ ⊗ Q agree. In particular, if m ∈ (M(L) ∩ G(O_L))p^{υ_2}(M(L) ∩ G(O_L)), then ν_m and ῡ_2^M have the same image in π_1(M)_Q.
items.note: Cited black box. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Weak admissibility of toral filtrations ([RZ, Prop. 1.21])
items.statement: As used in (2.2.3): if T ⊂ I_p ⊂ J_δ is a maximal Q_p-torus and μ_T ∈ X_*(T) is conjugate to μ with μ̄^T_T = ν_δ^{-1}, then μ_T^{-1} induces a (weakly) admissible filtration on 𝔻(𝒢_x)_K, where K is the field of definition of μ_T. It is admissible by Colmez–Fontaine.
items.note: Cited black box. The exact form of [RZ, 1.21] is not reproduced in lr.pdf; this is the statement as the paper uses it. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Special point; Mumford–Tate group
items.statement: A point of Sh_K(G,X) given by (h,g) is special if h: S → G_R factors through a Q-torus of G, equivalently if the Mumford–Tate group of h (the smallest Q-subgroup whose R-points contain h(S)) is a torus. For Hodge type, the Mumford–Tate group of 𝒜_x̃ is contained in G.
items.note: This is the target notion of Theorem (2.2.3) and Theorem (0.4), cf. [De 2]. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Elliptic element; stable conjugacy as used in (2.3.1)
items.statement: γ_0 ∈ G(R) is elliptic if it lies in a maximal R-torus of G that is anisotropic modulo the centre. In (2.3.1)(3) this is verified as γ_0 ∈ T(Q) with T(R)/w_h(R^×) compact. In (2.3.1)(2), 'stably conjugate to γ_p in G(Q̄_p)' means conjugate in G(Q̄_p).
items.note: K01 uses these notions for Kottwitz triples. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Steinberg's theorem over Q_p^ur
items.statement: H^1(Q_p^ur, H) = 0 for every connected linear algebraic group H over Q_p^ur. In (2.3.5) it is used to choose 𝔻(𝒢_x) ⊗_{K_0} Q_p^ur ≅ V*_{Q_p^ur} taking s_{α,0,x} to s_α and compatible with the action of T.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary (2.3.5), p. 34; also §4.3.6, p.77; also Proof of Lemma 4.5.6, p.89 (cited)
items.note: Cited black box. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Neutral gerb of a linear algebraic group
items.statement: If G is a linear algebraic group over k, the semidirect product 𝔊_G := G(k′) ⋊ Gal(k′/k) is the neutral k′/k-gerb attached to G. A k̄/k-Galois gerb is called a Galois gerb over k, and 𝔊^Δ is sometimes written for G(k̄). A k′/k-gerb gives a Galois gerb by pulling back along Gal(k̄/k) → Gal(k′/k) and pushing out along G(k′) → G(k̄). Every Galois gerb arises in this way from a k′/k-gerb with k′/k finite Galois.
items.note: Used everywhere (𝔊_G, 𝔊_T, 𝔊_{R_{L/Q}G_m}). C01–C03 refer to it without defining it. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Localization 𝔊(v) of a Galois gerb over Q
items.statement: For a Galois gerb 𝔊 over Q and a place v of Q, 𝔊(v) is the Galois gerb over Q_v obtained by pulling back along Gal(Q̄_v/Q_v) → Gal(Q̄/Q) (via the fixed embedding Q̄ ↪ Q̄_v) and pushing out along 𝔊^Δ(Q̄) → 𝔊^Δ(Q̄_v). A morphism f of Galois gerbs over Q induces f(v) in the same way.
items.note: Used in the definition of quasi-motivic gerbs (ζ_v: 𝔊_v → 𝔔(v)) and of admissibility (φ(v)∘ζ_v). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Local cocharacters of ψ_μ (3.1.11)–(3.1.12)
items.statement: Let T be a Q-torus, μ ∈ X_*(T) defined over a finite Galois extension L/Q in Q̄, and ψ_μ: 𝔔 → 𝔊_T as in (3.1.10). Write ν(p)_n for ν(p) viewed as a cocharacter with source D_n = G_m. If n = [L_p:Q_p], then ψ_μ^Δ∘ν(p)_n = Σ_{τ∈Gal(L_p/Q_p)} τ(μ). Hence, viewing ν(p) as a fractional cocharacter with source D_1, ψ_μ^Δ∘ν(p) = [L_p:Q_p]^{−1} Σ_{τ∈Gal(L_p/Q_p)} τ(μ) (3.1.11). If L_∞ = C, then ψ_μ^Δ∘ν(∞) = −Σ_{τ∈Gal(L_∞/R)} τ(μ) (3.1.12).
items.note: Used in the proofs of Lemma 3.4.1 (3.1.12), Lemma 3.4.2 ((3.1.11), (3.4.4)) and Lemma 3.5.8. I checked both formulas against the definitions of ψ^L and ν(v)^L. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Frobenius element d_σ of the unramified gerb 𝔇
items.statement: Let σ ∈ Gal(Q_p^ur/Q_p) be the Frobenius and Q_{p^n} ⊂ Q̄_p the unramified extension of degree n. There is an element d_σ ∈ 𝔇 with image σ such that, for every n ≥ 1, the image of d_σ^n in 𝔊_p^{Q_{p^n}} is p^{−1} ∈ 𝔊_p^{Q_{p^n},Δ}.
items.note: This fixes the normalization θ^{ur,Δ} = −ν_b used in the proofs of 3.4.2 and 3.5.8. It is also used to define b_g, X_p(θ) and Φ. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: p^r-Frobenius Φ on X_p(θ)
items.statement: Suppose E_p = Q_{p^r}. The Frobenius Φ = Φ_r on X_p(θ) is defined by θ^ur_{Φ(g)} = Int(1⋊σ^r)∘θ^ur_g (read on d_σ; see the sourceIssue). Explicitly, b_{Φ(g)} = σ^r(b_g) ∈ G(Z_p^ur)p^{−μ}G(Z_p^ur) and Φ(g) = g b_g σ(b_g)⋯σ^{r−1}(b_g).
items.note: Lemma 3.3.4 (R03) and Conjecture 3.3.7 refer to it. R1's S04 is the ADLV analogue, not this definition. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Unramified representative of a local gerb morphism [LR, §5]
items.statement: [LR, §5, p. 56] For a morphism θ: 𝔊_p → 𝔊_G(p), there exists g_0 ∈ G(Q̄_p) such that Int(g_0^{−1})∘θ is induced by a morphism of Q_p^ur/Q_p-gerbs θ^ur: 𝔇 → 𝔊^ur_G(p). One writes θ^ur(d_σ) = b_{g_0} ⋊ σ.
items.note: Black box from another paper. It is used for Lemma 3.3.4, for (3.3.6)(3), in the proof of 3.4.2 and, for tori, in the proof of 3.5.8. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Local comparison morphisms ξ_v and I_{ξ_∞} = G*_R
items.statement: Let (G,X) be a Shimura datum and h ∈ X. Choose w ∈ 𝔊_∞ lifting complex conjugation c with w^2 = −1 ∈ 𝔊_∞^Δ(C) = C^×. Then ξ_∞: 𝔊_∞ → 𝔊_G(∞) is the morphism that is w_h on 𝔊_∞^Δ and sends w to μ_h(−1)⋊c (cf. [Re, §B3]). Since conjugation by μ_h(−1) is a Cartan involution of G and w_h is central, I_{ξ_∞} = G*_R, the inner form of G_R with compact adjoint group. For v ≠ p, ∞, ξ_v: 𝔊_v → 𝔊_G(v) is τ ↦ 1⋊τ.
items.note: R04 mentions ξ_∞ only in passing. The identification I_{ξ_∞} = G*_R is used in (3.4.13). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Standing hyperspecial setup and the cocharacter μ
items.statement: (G,X) is a Shimura datum with reflex field E ⊂ Q̄ ⊂ C, and G_{Q_p} has a reductive model G_{Z_p} over Z_p. By [Ki 2, 2.3.2], G_{Z_p} arises from a reductive model G_{Z_(p)} of G over Z_(p). The existence of G_{Z_p} implies that p is unramified in E, so E_p = Q_{p^r} is unramified. μ_h is conjugate to a cocharacter μ that is defined over E_p and induces a cocharacter of G_{Z_p}.
items.note: Fixes the μ used in admissibility conditions (1) and (3). [Ki 2, 2.3.2] is a black box from another paper. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: X^p(φ) is a G(A_f^p)-torsor [Re, B3.6]
items.statement: If φ: 𝔔 → 𝔊_G satisfies (3.3.6)(2), then X^p(φ) = {(g_l)_{l≠∞,p} ∈ G(Ā_f^p) : Int(g_l)∘ξ_l = φ(l)∘ζ_l} is non-empty, by (3.1.7)(2) and [Re, B3.6]. Here Ā_f^p = Π′ Q̄_l. Hence X^p(φ) is a G(A_f^p)-torsor.
items.note: Black box from another paper. It is needed for the structure of S(φ) and S_τ(φ). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: S(φ) with its Hecke and Frobenius actions
items.statement: For admissible φ, I_φ = Aut(φ) acts on X(φ) := X_p(φ) × X^p(φ) by left multiplication. S(φ) := lim_{K^p} I_φ(Q)\X_p(φ)×X^p(φ)/K^p, with K^p running over compact open subgroups of G(A_f^p). It carries an action of Z_G(Q_p) × G(A_f^p) and a commuting action of the Frobenius Φ.
items.note: R05 records S_τ(φ) but not the untwisted S(φ) with its actions, which is the right-hand side of Conjecture 3.3.7 (M08). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Cocharacters of the Weil torus (3.5.2)
items.statement: For a q-Weil number π, let χ_π ∈ X^*(P^L) be the corresponding character. P^L carries cocharacters ν(∞)^L and ν(p)^L characterized by ⟨ν(v)^L, χ_π⟩ = log_q | Π_{τ∈Gal(L_v/Q_v)} τ(π) |_v for v = ∞, p. The map X^*(P^L) → Z^{Gal(L/Q)}, χ ↦ (⟨τ(ν(p)^L), χ⟩)_τ, is injective, so X^*(P^L) is finitely generated and P^L is a torus.
items.note: Q09 and Q10 use these cocharacters without defining them. I checked that they satisfy the relation in Lemma 3.5.3 (using ππ̄ = q^ι). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Galois action on the Dynkin diagram factors through a CM field [De 2, 2.3.4(b)]
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (H,Y) with H adjoint, the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on the Dynkin diagram of H factors through Gal(L/Q) for a CM field L.
items.note: Black box from another paper. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Admissible morphisms are special when G^der is simply connected [LR, Satz 5.3]
items.statement: If (G,X) is a Shimura datum with G^der simply connected and hyperspecial level at p, then every admissible morphism that factors through the pseudo-motivic gerb 𝔓 is special (conjugate to i∘ψ_{μ_{h_T}} for a special pair (T, h_T)).
items.note: This is the main black box of §3.5. Kisin combines it with Lemma 3.5.7 to get factorization through 𝔓. His normalization of ψ is the inverse of LR's (footnote 13). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Lift of an adjoint Shimura datum with simply connected derived group and compact center
items.statement: Let (H,Y) be a Shimura datum with H adjoint. There is a Shimura datum (G,X) with (G^ad, X^ad) = (H,Y), G^der = H̃ simply connected, and Z_{G,R} a compact torus, so that Z_G satisfies the Serre condition. Construction: embed Z_{H̃} ↪ S_L^n, where S_L = ker(N_{L/L_0}: R_{L/Q}G_m → R_{L_0/Q}G_m); set G = (H̃ × S_L^n)/Z_{H̃}; lift h ∈ Y, which factors through 𝕊/𝕊_0, to h̃: 𝕊/𝕊_0 → G; take X to be the G(R)-conjugacy class of h̃.
items.note: This is the key reduction step of Theorem 3.5.11. To apply §3 to (G,X), L must also be chosen unramified at p; see the sourceIssues. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Kernel of κ̃_G on unramified and rational points
items.statement: Let G_{Z_p} be reductive, ρ: G̃ → G. Then ρ(G̃(Q_p^ur))·G_{Z_p}(Z_p^ur) = ker(κ̃_G: G(Q_p^ur) → π_1(G)), a normal subgroup; ρ(G̃(Q_p^ur))·G_{Z_p}(Z_p^ur) ∩ G(Q_p) = ρ(G̃(Q_p))·G_{Z_p}(Z_p) = ker(κ̃_G|_{G(Q_p)}); and a class in G(Q_p^ur)/ρ(G̃(Q_p^ur))G(Z_p^ur) with Frobenius-invariant κ̃_G-image contains an element of G(Q_p) (via (1.2.3)).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 3.6.2(2), p.54 ('The Cartan decomposition implies'); used in (3.6.8)–(3.6.9), p.58
items.note: Unnumbered fact, justified only by 'the Cartan decomposition'. It gives the simple transitivity on X_p(φ_ab~) and the maps (3.6.9). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Toric maps to the component sets (3.6.9)
items.statement: For a Q-torus T, h_T: S → T_R, µ_T = µ_{h_T}, and i: T → G with i∘h_T ∈ X: t ↦ [i∘h_T, i(t)] gives T(Q)^-\T(A_f) → 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C) → π(G,X), inducing (3.6.9) T(Q)^-\T(A_f)/𝒯°(Z_p) → π(G,X), because i(𝒯°(Z_p)) ⊂ ker κ̃_G|_{G(Q_p)} = G̃(Q_p)G(Z_p). Likewise (t,(g_l)) ↦ (i(t), (i(g_l),1)) induces S(ψ_{µ_T}) → π(G, i∘ψ_{µ_T}) = π(G,(i∘ψ_{µ_T})^ad), using i(𝒯°(Z_p^ur)) ⊂ G̃(Q_p^ur)G(Z_p^ur).
items.note: These are the right and left vertical maps of (3.6.11); no item defines them. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Geometric component set π(G,X) and its π(G)-torsor structure
items.statement: For (G,X) ∈ SH_p with K_p = G_{Z_(p)}(Z_p): π(G,X) := π_0(𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C)), where 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(C) = lim_{K^p} G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K_pK^p. Right multiplication makes π(G,X) a π(G)-torsor, π(G) = G(Q)^-_+\G(A_f)/G_{Z_p}(Z_p) [De 2, 2.1.3]. Under G(Q)\π_0(X) × G(A_f)/K_p ≅ G(Q)^-_+\G(A_f)/K_p (limit over K^p), the class of (g_1·X^+, 1), g_1 ∈ G(R), is g_2^{-1} for any g_2 ∈ G(Q) with the same image as g_1 in G(R)/G(R)_+.
items.locator: §3.6.8, p.57; used in the proof of 3.6.10, p.59
items.note: Cited from [De 2, 2.1.3]. Here G(R)_+ must be the preimage of G^ad(R)^+ (the proof uses G(R)_+ ⊃ Z_G(R)G̃(R)). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Right action of the integral adjoint group on S_τ(G,φ_0) (Lemma 3.7.2)
items.statement: (3.7.1) G(Z̄_(p))^♮_+ := preimage in G(Q̄) of G^ad(Z_(p))^+ = G^ad_{Z_(p)}(Z_(p)) ∩ G^ad(Q)^+. Lemma 3.7.2: right multiplication defines an action of G(Z̄_(p))^♮_+ on ∐_{φ^ad=φ_0} X(φ) (unrefined X(φ) = X_p(φ) × X^p(φ), φ admissible lifts of φ_0), g mapping X(φ) bijectively onto X(z^{-1}·φ), z_τ = g^{-1}τ(g) ∈ Z^1(Q,Z_G), and on X_p it keeps b_{g_0g} ∈ G(Z_p^ur)p^{−µ}G(Z_p^ur). This induces a right action of G^ad(Z_(p))^+ on S_τ(G,φ_0) (Z_G(Q̄) ⊂ I_{φ_0}(Q̄)^♮ acts trivially).
items.note: R24's locator names this lemma, but its statement does not contain it. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Away-from-p description of π(G) (3.7.5)
items.statement: The natural map G(Z_(p))^-_+\G(A^p_f) → G(Q)^-_+\G(A_f)/G_{Z_p}(Z_p) = π(G) is a bijection [Ki 2, 3.3.3]. Hence A(G_{Z_(p)})/A(G_{Z_(p)})° ≅ G(A^p_f)/G(Z_(p))^-_+ ≅ π(G).
items.note: Black box from [Ki 2]. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: A(G)° depends only on G^der
items.statement: If G_{Z_(p)} → G_{2,Z_(p)} induces isomorphisms G^der ≅ G_2^der and on adjoint groups, the induced map A(G_{Z_(p)})° → A(G_{2,Z_(p)})° is an isomorphism [Ki 2, 3.3.2], [De 2, 2.0.12]. A° is functorial for central isogenies of derived groups (used in 3.8.10, 3.8.12).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 3.8.2, p.63; proof of Lemma 3.8.5, p.65 (there cited as [Ki 2, 3.3.7])
items.note: Black box. The same fact is cited as [Ki 2, 3.3.2] on p.63 and [Ki 2, 3.3.7] on p.65; one of these numbers is probably a slip (not checkable here). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: A(G)-action on Sh_{K_p} and the component map (3.7.7)
items.statement: (3.7.6) By [De 2, §2.7], Sh_{K_p}(G,X) carries an action of A(G_{Z_(p)}) extending the G(A^p_f)-action, and Sh_{K_p}(G,X)(C) → π(G,X) is A(G)-equivariant (A(G) acting through A(G) → π(G)). If Sh_{K_p}(G,X) has an integral canonical model 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X) [Mi 2], there is an induced A(G)-equivariant map (3.7.7) 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(F̄_p) → π(G,X) identifying the geometrically connected components of 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X) with π(G,X); 𝒮_{K_p} exists for (G,X) of abelian type and p > 2 [Ki 2]. Φ is the geometric r-Frobenius on 𝒮_{K_p}(G,X)(F̄_p).
items.note: The vertical left arrow of Conjecture 3.7.8 (M08). It is a construction together with cited results. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: G(Z_p)·G(Q)^+ = G(Q_p)
items.statement: For G_{Z_(p)} reductive, G_{Z_p}(Z_p)·G(Q)^+ = G(Q_p) [Ki 2, 2.2.6] (cf. [Sa, Cor. 3.5]).
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Decomposition of the closure of G(Q)_+
items.statement: [De 2, 2.0.13] as used: every g_2 ∈ G_2(Q)^-_+ (closure in G_2(A_f)) can be written g_2 = j_2g′_2z_2 with g′_2 ∈ G_2(Q)_+, j_2 ∈ G_2^der(Q)^-_+ and z_2 ∈ Z_{G_2}(Q)^-.
items.note: Black box; the Deligne numbering is not checked here. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Lang's lemma for smooth connected integral groups
items.statement: For a smooth affine group scheme H over Z_p with connected fibres, H^1(Gal(Q_p^ur/Q_p), H(Z_p^ur)) = 1 (every H-torsor over Z_p is trivial); likewise over Z_l.
items.locator: footnote 20, p.54; proof of Prop 3.6.7, p.57; Remark 3.7.10(2), p.62; proof of Lemma 3.8.2, p.63; also §4.3.6 (p.77) and §4.3.10 (p.79)
items.note: Only unramified cocycles are covered (this is the point of the §3.6.1 issue). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Integral z-extensions
items.statement: [Ko 6, §1]: G_{Z_(p)} admits a z-extension G_{1,Z_(p)} → G_{Z_(p)}, a surjection of reductive Z_(p)-groups with central induced-torus kernel and G_1^der simply connected. X lifts to a G_1(R)-class X_1, and each triple (T,h,i) lifts to (T_1,h_1,i_1).
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Triviality of the limit of idele class groups
items.statement: lim_L (L^×)^-\(L⊗_QA)^×/(L⊗_QR)^{×,+} = 1, over finite L ⊂ Q̄ with norm transition maps (class field theory), and hence C := lim_L (L^×)^-\(L⊗A_f)^×/(O_L⊗Z_p)^× = 1.
items.note: Gives S(ψ) = {1} and the canonical trivialization of S(ψ_{µ_T}). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Moduli tuple on a Shimura subdatum and its Z_{G'}-action
items.statement: Let V be as in (1.3.2) and (G',X') ↪ (G,X) ↪ (GSp,S^±) embeddings of Shimura data, with (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗ defining G. Let K' ⊂ G'(A_f), K ⊂ G(A_f) be compact open with Sh_{K'}(G',X') ↪ Sh_K(G,X), E' the reflex field of (G',X'), T an E'-scheme and x ∈ Sh_{K'}(G',X')(T). Attached to x is a tuple (A, λ, ε_{K'}) [Ki 2, 3.2.4]: A an abelian scheme up to isogeny over T, λ a weak polarization, and ε_{K'} ∈ Γ(T, Isom(V_{A_f}, V̂(A)_Q)/K'), which respects polarizations up to a scalar and takes s_α to (s_{α,l,x})_l of (1.3.6). By [Ki 2, 3.2.2], A carries a natural action of Z_{G'}.
items.note: Black-box input from [Ki 2]. Lemma 4.2.4 (T09) and the construction of i_ω rely on it. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Twisted morphism i_ω into the Siegel Shimura variety
items.statement: Let ω ∈ (G/Z_{G'})(Q)_1 with lift ω̃ ∈ G(F), and P the fibre of G → G/Z_{G'} over ω (a Z_{G'}-torsor). Apply §4.1 with Z = Z_{G'} to the tuple (A, λ, ε_{K'}) of (4.2.3); ε_{K'} is Z_{G'}-compatible by (4.2.4). This gives (A^P, λ^P, ε^ω_{K'^ω}) with K'^ω = ω̃K'ω̃^{-1}, and hence a morphism i_ω: Sh_{K'}(G',X') → Sh_{K^ψ_ω}(GSp,S^±) for some compact open K^ψ_ω ⊂ GSp(A_f).
items.note: Prop. 4.2.6 (T10) is a statement about this morphism, but the morphism itself has no item. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Integral twisting maps and the A(G_{Z(p)})-action on S_{K_p}(G,X)
items.statement: Setting of (1.3.3): K = K_pK^p, K_p = G_{Z(p)}(Z_p) hyperspecial, G ↪ GSp induced by G_{Z(p)} ↪ GL(V_{Z(p)}). For ω ∈ G^ad(Z_(p))^+ (3.7.1), the construction of (4.2.5) with (G',X') = (G,X) gives i_ω: Sh_K(G,X) → Sh_{K^ω}(G,X), K^ω = K_pK^{pω}. By the extension property this extends to a map of O_(p)-schemes i_ω: S_K(G,X) → S_{K^ω}(G,X). Letting ω act via i_{ω^{-1}} turns this into a right action of G^ad(Z_(p))^+ and equips S_{K_p}(G,X) with an action of A(G_{Z(p)}) = G(A_f^p) *_{G(Z(p))_+} G^ad(Z_(p))^+. For an O_(p)-scheme T and x ∈ S_K(G,X)(T), let P_{Z(p)} be the fibre of G_{Z(p)} → G^ad_{Z(p)} over ω (a Z_{G_{Z(p)}}-torsor) and P = P_{Z(p)} ⊗ Q. Then A_{i_ω(x)} (an abelian scheme up to prime-to-p isogeny), viewed up to isogeny, is canonically A_x^P. It suffices to check this at the tautological point: over T ⊗ Q it holds by construction, and it extends over T by [FC, 2.7].
items.note: Lemma 4.2.9 (T11) and Prop. 4.4.14 (K18) use this action and the identification A_{i_ω(x)} = A_x^P; neither has its own item. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Uniqueness of the global inner form I of a Kottwitz triple
items.statement: By the Hasse principle for adjoint groups, the inner twisting I of I_0 in (4.3.1)(iv) is uniquely determined. If I and I' both satisfy (iv), there is an isomorphism I ≅ I', canonical up to conjugation by I^ad(Q), which intertwines the inner twistings with I_0.
items.note: The proof of Prop. 4.4.13 uses this ('we saw in (4.3.1) that there is an isomorphism I ≅ I' as inner twists of I_{γ0}'). It rests on the black box hasse-principle-adjoint-groups. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Transport of a refinement along an equivalence of triples
items.statement: Let k ~ k' with representatives of the same level r, δ' = g0δσ(g0)^{-1} and (γ_l')_{l≠p} = g^pγ_lg^{p-1}, where g^p ∈ G(A_f^p) and g0 ∈ G(K_0). If k̃ = (γ0,(γ_l),δ,ι) refines k, then I'_{A_f} = (g0,g^p)I_{A_f}(g0,g^p)^{-1} as subgroups of G(L) × G(A_f^p). ι' := Int(g0,g^p)∘ι makes k̃' = (γ0',(γ_l'),δ',ι') a refinement of k'; it depends on the choice of (g0,g^p). Left multiplication by (g0,g^p) is a bijection X_υ(δ) × G(A_f^p) → X_υ(δ') × G(A_f^p) (4.3.3). It is I-equivariant for the actions through ι and ι', so it induces S(k̃) ≅ S(k̃').
items.note: Prop. 4.4.17's proof uses this ('composing with multiplication on the left by h̃g_{x'}^{-1} as in (4.3.2)'). K04 covers only the equivalence relation. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Refined twist by the class of an element of G^ad(Q)^+
items.statement: Let k̃ = (γ0,(γ_l),δ,ι) refine k, and let β be the image of h ∈ G^ad(Q)^+ under G^ad(Q) → H^1(Q,Z_G) → H^1(Q,I). Then β is trivial in H^1(Q,I^ad), so I is also the inner twisting attached to k^β. For any lift h̃ ∈ G(Q̄) of h, k^β = (γ0, (h̃γ_lh̃^{-1})_{l≠p}, h̃δh̃^{-1}). As a triple (not just up to equivalence), this does not depend on h̃. Moreover I_{A_f}(k^β) = h̃I_{A_f}h̃^{-1} ⊂ G(L) × G(A_f^p). The refined twist k̃^β uses the isomorphism I ⊗_Q A_f ≅ I_{A_f}(k^β) given by ι followed by conjugation by h̃.
items.note: Props. 4.4.17 (K19, K20) use this refined twist, S(k̃(x)^β). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Comparison element g_{x'} for points of a central twist
items.statement: Let h ∈ G^ad(Q)^+, P the corresponding Z_G-torsor, β ∈ H^1(Q,Z_G) the class of P, and h̃ ∈ P(F) a lift of h (F/Q finite), so that z_τ = h̃^{-1}τ(h̃) represents β. Fix D(G_x) ≅ V^*_{Z(p)} ⊗_{Z(p)} W taking s_{α,0,x} to s_α, as in (2.1.2). For x' ∈ I_x^β, the natural isomorphism A_{x'} ⊗_Q F ≅ A_x ⊗_Q F induced by h̃ identifies D(A_{x'}) with g_0^{-1}D(A_x) for some g_0 ∈ G(L ⊗_Q F) with g_0^{-1}τ(g_0) = z_τ. The isomorphism V_{A_f} ⊗ F ≅ V_{A_f} ⊗ F induced by ε_{x'} and ε_x is multiplication by (g^p)^{-1} on V_{A_f^p}, where g^p ∈ G(A_f^p ⊗_Q F) also has cocycle z_τ. Set g_{x'} = (g_0, g^p).
items.note: Defines the element in the formula x' ↦ h̃g_{x'}^{-1} and in the component formula of Prop. 4.4.17. The printed 'z_τ = g_0^{-1}τ(g)' is corrected here (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Real Galois cohomology of a compact group (Serre)
items.statement: [Se, III §4.5, Thm. 6] Let H be a connected reductive group over R with H(R) compact. Then H^1(R,H) is identified with the set of H(R)-conjugacy classes of elements of order dividing 2 in H(R) (H[2]/H), functorially in H.
items.note: Black box behind Lemma 4.4.5 (H09). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: σ-conjugacy classes in a p-adic torus (Kottwitz)
items.statement: [Ko 2, 2.5] For a torus T over Q_p, σ-conjugacy classes of T(Q̂_p^ur) are classified by their image in X_*(T)_{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} (the Kottwitz map). For μ ∈ X_*(T) defined over L_p and π a uniformizer of L_p, N_{L_p/L_{p,0}}(μ(π)) maps to the image of μ.
items.note: Black box that gives the σ-conjugacy of δ and δ' in Lemma 4.3.11 (K11). Planned: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1 plans the Kottwitz and Newton invariants and their relation for tori.

items.name: Global points with local conditions (Moret-Bailly)
items.statement: [MB, Thm. 1.3] Used as follows. If a Z_G-torsor P over Q (Z_G a torus, G unramified at p) acquires a point over an unramified extension of Q_p, then P(F) ≠ ∅ for some finite Galois F/Q in which p is unramified.
items.note: Black box for the second assertion of Prop. 4.4.17 (K20); footnote 24 explains why. Planned: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly's theorem with prescribed local conditions.

items.name: Extension of homomorphisms of abelian schemes over a normal base (Faltings–Chai)
items.statement: [FC, I.2.7] Let S be a normal noetherian scheme, U ⊂ S dense open, and A, B abelian schemes over S. Every homomorphism A_U → B_U extends uniquely to a homomorphism A → B. In particular a quasi-isogeny, or an identification up to isogeny, over the generic fibre extends over S.
items.note: Used to extend the identification A_{i_ω(x)} = A_x^P from S_K(G,X) ⊗ Q to S_K(G,X). The paper cites '[FC, 2.7]'. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Hasse principle for adjoint groups
items.statement: If H is an adjoint (connected semisimple) group over Q, then H^1(Q,H) → Π_v H^1(Q_v,H) is injective. Consequently an inner form of a connected reductive group over Q is determined up to isomorphism by its localizations at all places.
items.locator: §4.3.1, p.75; also Proof of Corollary 4.6.5, p.94 (cited)
items.note: Black box for the uniqueness of I. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Shimura–Taniyama reciprocity for the Frobenius of CM points
items.statement: Let x̃, x̃' be CM points whose abelian varieties carry actions of the same torus T, with Hodge cocharacters given by the same μ_T. Then for r sufficiently large, the geometric p^r-Frobenius on the l-adic and crystalline cohomology of their reductions A_x and A_{x'} is given by one element γ ∈ T(Q).
items.note: Cited only as 'the reciprocity law'. Planned: ShimuraVarieties V5 plans the Shimura–Taniyama Frobenius calculation for CM abelian varieties.

items.name: Correction element y_φ
items.statement: In the setting of (4.5.1) (φ admissible, g = (g_0,g^p) ∈ X(φ), c ∈ P^L(Q̂_p^ur) as in (4.3.9), c' ∈ P^L(Q_{p^n}) with θ^ur_{g_0}(c'c^{-1}) ∈ G(Ẑ_p^ur)), put y_φ = φ^Δ(p)(c^{-1}c') × 1 ∈ G(Q̂_p^ur) × G(A_f^p). Then g_0^{-1} y_φ g_0 = θ^ur_{g_0}(c^{-1}c') ∈ G(Ẑ_p^ur), so y_φ acts trivially on π(G,φ_0).
items.locator: §4.5.1, last line, p.88; property used p.93
items.note: Appears in the maps g' ↦ g^{-1}y_φg' of 4.5.2, 4.5.4, 4.5.9, 4.5.11 and in the proof of 4.6.2. The paper prints y_φ ∈ G(Ẑ_p^ur) × G(A_f^p); see source issues. y_φ depends on the choice of c', hence on g_0. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Refinements k̃(g) and k̃(g,τ) of the gerb triple
items.statement: For φ admissible and g ∈ X(φ), the natural action of I_φ on X(φ) gives a canonical refinement k̃(g) = (γ_0,(γ_l),δ,ι) of k(g), with ι: I_φ ⊗ A_f ≅ I_{A_f}(k(φ)) the natural isomorphism. For τ ∈ I_φ^ad(A_f), k̃(g,τ) is the refinement whose isomorphism is ι composed with conjugation by τ.
items.note: Used in 4.5.4, 4.5.9, 4.5.11, 4.6.2. K21 and K23 mention these objects, but no item defines them. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Twist φ^β of an admissible morphism
items.statement: By (3.1.2), conjugacy classes of φ': Q → G_G with φ'^Δ = φ^Δ are in bijection with H^1(Q,I), I = I_φ, via z ↦ z·φ, (z·φ)(q) = z_τ φ(q) for q over τ. For β ∈ H^1(Q,I), φ^β denotes a representative of the corresponding class. For h ∈ G^ad(Q)^+ with lift h̃ ∈ G(Q̄) and β the associated class (from H^1(Q,Z_G)), one takes φ^β = z·φ with z_τ = h̃^{-1}τ(h̃).
items.note: Used in 4.5.6, 4.5.7, 4.5.11, 4.6.2, 4.6.5. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Isogeny classes and admissible morphisms attached to (T,h_T,i); the set I_0
items.statement: Let (T,h_T,i) be as in (3.5.8). An isogeny class I ⊂ S_{K_p}(G,X)(F̄_p) is attached to (T,h_T,i) if the reductions mod p of the points in i(Sh(T,h_T)) ⊂ Sh_{K_p}(G,X) lie in I. An admissible φ: Q → G_G is attached to (T,h_T,i) if φ is conjugate to i∘ψ_{μ_{h_T}}. For fixed I, I_0 = ∪_{h∈G^ad(Q)^+} I^{[h]}, where [h] is the image of h in Ш^∞_G(Q,I) and I^β is the twisted isogeny class of (4.4.7).
items.note: The definitions behind M01 and M03. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Twisting a common special triple
items.statement: In §4.6, let I and φ both be attached to (T,h_T,i), and let β ∈ Ш^∞_G(Q,I) be represented by a cocycle z ∈ Z^1(Q,Z_I). Choose g ∈ G(Q̄) with g^{-1}τ(g) = z_τ, and put i^β = g i g^{-1}: T → G, which is defined over Q. Then i^β∘h_T ∈ X, and I^β and φ^β are both attached to (T,h_T,i^β). This applies to β = [h] for h ∈ G^ad(Q)^+, and to every β ∈ Ш_G(Q,I) (such β come from Z^1(Q,Z_I) by the Hasse principle for I^ad).
items.note: An unnumbered claim that carries the proof of 4.6.5. It needs z_τ ∈ T(Q̄), i.e. Z_I ⊂ i(T); see the new gap entry. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [LR, Lem. 5.4]: rationality of φ(δ_n)
items.statement: If φ: Q → G_G is admissible and factors through P^L, then for n divisible by a suitable integer m and sufficiently large, φ(δ_n) ∈ G(Q̄) is G(Q̄)-conjugate to an element γ_0 ∈ G(Q).
items.note: Black box. Footnote 25 notes that §3.5 gives more (φ is conjugate to a special morphism, 3.5.11), and 3.5.11 would give it directly: γ_0 = i(ψ^Δ(δ_n)) ∈ i(T(Q)). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [Ko 4, Lem. 12.1] with Shimura–Taniyama reciprocity
items.statement: If x ∈ S_{K_p}(G,X)(F̄_p) is the reduction of a point of i(Sh(T,h_T)) for a special datum (T,h_T,i), then the Kottwitz triple k(x) is equivalent to i_* of the triple k'(T,h_T) built from N(μ_{h_T}) in (4.3.9)/(4.3.10). Concretely, k(x) = (γ_0,(γ_l)_{l≠p},δ) with γ_l = γ_0 ∈ i(T(Q)).
items.locator: §4.6.1 and proof of Proposition 4.6.2, p.92 (cited; cf. [Wi 3, 4.2.5])
items.note: Black box behind M01(a). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [Ki 2, 3.4.13] (from [De 2]): the cover H♯ of an adjoint abelian-type datum
items.statement: For (H,Y) of abelian type with H adjoint, there is a central isogeny H♯ → H such that (1) every Hodge-type (G,X) with (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (H,Y) has G^der a quotient of H♯; and (2) there is a Hodge-type (G,X) with (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (H,Y) and G^der = H♯; if H is quasi-split and unramified at p, G can be chosen quasi-split and unramified at p.
items.note: Black box behind M05/M06, apart from the Z_G-torus and reflex-field refinements. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [KP, 4.6.22]: Hodge-type cover with torus centre
items.statement: The Hodge-type datum (G,X) in Lemma 4.6.6(2) can be chosen with Z_G a torus.
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [De 2, 2.3.10]: Hodge-type datum from H♯ and a CM torus
items.statement: For H = R_{F/Q}H^s Q-simple adjoint of abelian type (F totally real, H^s absolutely simple, [De 2, 2.3.4]), a totally imaginary quadratic K/F and h_T: S → (K ⊗_Q R)^× of the type chosen in the proof, Deligne's construction gives a Hodge-type (G,X) with G^der = H♯ and (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (H,Y), whose reflex field is contained in E(H,Y)·E(R_{K/Q}G_m, h_T).
items.note: Black box. The paper uses it to get E(G,X)_p = E(G^ad,X^ad)_p. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [Ki 2, 3.4.14]: integral model of the Hodge-type cover
items.statement: In the situation of the proof of Theorem 4.6.7 (G quasi-split and unramified at p, a central isogeny G^der → G_2^der inducing (G^ad,X^ad) ≅ (G_2^ad,X_2^ad), and G_{2,Z(p)} a reductive model of G_2), there are a reductive model G_{Z(p)} of G over Z_(p) and a central isogeny G^der_{Z(p)} → G^der_{2,Z(p)} extending G^der → G_2^der.
items.note: Black box. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [Ki 2, 3.4.11] as repaired by Errata E.5–E.7: abelian-type integral model as a quotient
items.statement: Let p > 2. With (G,X), G_{Z(p)} → G_{2,Z(p)} as above and X^+ ⊂ X ∩ X_2, the quotient S_{K_{2,p}}(G_2,X_2) = [A(G_{2,Z(p)}) × S_{K_p}(G,X)^+]/A(G_{Z(p)})° is well defined and is an integral canonical model of Sh_{K_{2,p}}(G_2,X_2) over O_{E(G_2,X_2)_p}, with its A(G_{2,Z(p)})-action.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.6.7, p.95; Errata (E.5.1), p.96 (cited)
items.note: Black box behind M07. Its original proof used the false finiteness in [Ki 2, 3.3.9] (source issue E3); E06 and E07 give the replacement argument. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: [De 2, 2.0.4]-type finiteness of locally trivial central torsors
items.statement: For the centre Z_G of the reductive group G_{Z(p)}, the kernel of H^1(Z_(p), Z_G) → ∏_{l≠p} H^1(Q_l, Z_G) is finite.
items.note: Black box behind E06. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Kottwitz and Newton invariants agree for tori [RR, 4.2(ii)]
items.statement: For a torus T over Q_p and b ∈ T(Q_p^ur), the image of κ_T(b) ∈ X_*(T)_Γ in X_*(T)_Γ ⊗ Q ≅ X_*(T)^Γ_Q is ν_b.
items.locator: proof of Lemma (3.4.2), (3.4.4), p. 46; also proof of Proposition 3.6.7, p.57 (also used in 3.4.2)
items.note: Black box. For T = R_{L/Q}G_m, X_*(T)_Γ is torsion-free, so the rational identity gives (3.4.4). Check against R1's B02 before adding it separately. Planned: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1 plans the Kottwitz and Newton invariants and their relation for tori.

items.name: Kneser: H^1 of simply connected groups over p-adic fields
items.statement: If G̃ is a simply connected semisimple group over Q_l with l a finite prime, then H^1(Q_l, G̃) = 0.
items.locator: proof of Proposition (3.4.11), p. 48; also proofs of Lemma 3.6.2(2) (p.54: 'the class of ε_l ∈ H^1(Q_l,G̃) is trivial'), Corollary 3.6.4 (p.55) and Proposition 3.6.10 (p.59); also §4.4.9, p.82; also Proof of Lemma 4.5.6, p.89 (implicit: trivial in H^1(Q_l, G̃→G) implies trivial in H^1(Q_l,G)); proof of Lemma 4.6.4, p.93
items.note: Standard black box. With it, condition (3.3.6)(2) at finite v ≠ p holds automatically for the lifts z·φ. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Real approximation
items.statement: For a connected algebraic group H over Q (in the uses here, G, G^ad, or the torus T/Z_{G̃}), H(Q) is dense in H(R).
items.locator: proofs of Lemma (3.4.8) p. 46, Proposition (3.4.11) p. 48, Lemma (3.5.10) p. 51; also proof of Lemma 3.6.2(3), p.55; proof of Proposition 3.6.10, p.59
items.note: Standard black box. It is used three times in §3.4–3.5. Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 plans strong approximation for simply connected groups and weak (in particular real) approximation.

routes.reason: Reuse the existing candidate in this direction; these are additional source obligations, not a second roadmap or implemented stages.
routes.brief: Reuse the KPZ26/KP18 tensor-display candidate. Import finite flat groups and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory), p-adic Hodge theory (PadicHodgeTheory), crystalline cohomology (CrystallineCohomology), SF.1 descent and RG2 integral reductive groups. Add the hyperspecial height-one Breuil–Kisin specialization as an explicit interface, not a duplicate classification. Build the integral tensor frame, adapted-lift predicate, formally smooth R_G and relative period comparison before Kisin1.1.13/1.1.19. End with Kisin1.2.18–1.2.19 lattice specialization, κ preservation and quotient compatibility, and1.4.6 integral connection along frame families. Apply E.1–E.4 to Kisin2010: Frobenius conjugation stability of Lie(H), delete1.5.3, use Lie(G), and identify the horizontal Fil0 locus with the adapted completion. Retain the linear dual/Cartier dual Tate twist and inverse filtration. Break relative comparison, connection convergence and adapted factorization into declaration-sized proofs. Test Gm lattice p, zero modules and wrong E² height. Do not use the false integral representative g0∈G(OL) in the printed proof. Corrections the design must carry: the isomorphism (1.1.14) of Proposition (1.1.13), and the step of (1.1.19) that uses it, need G_Z_p connected (E8); [Ki 2]'s T_p𝒢* is T_p𝒢*(−1) in (1.4.2), (1.4.3), (1.5.11) (footnote 8; E7).

routes.reason: Reuse the existing candidate in this direction; these are additional source obligations, not a second roadmap or implemented stages.
routes.brief: Reuse the HE21 ADLV candidate. Keep its cordial/dimension branch separate from this minuscule mixed-characteristic component branch. Import Hecke stacks and local shtukas (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas), geometric Satake and fusion (GeometricSatakeAndFusion) for affine Grassmannians, BG0/BG1 for B(G), J_b, κ and Newton, RG2 for integral cosets, and the tensor-display Part II for lifts. Define frame-family π0 and prove its comparison with whichever geometric component functor is used. Prove nonemptiness, relative-position loci, Hodge–Newton reduction and the corrected CKV component theorem in the adjoint Qp-simple HN-indecomposable minuscule case; retain the μ=0,b~1 discrete G(Qp)/G(Zp) exception. The paper uses [CKV, Theorem 1.1] (its Theorem 1.2.14) and Lemmas 2.1.4, 2.5.2, Proposition 2.5.4 and a corollary of Chen–Kisin–Viehmann as black boxes; their published proof is corrected by the 2017 corrigendum (Compositio 153), which the design must read, including its omitted D4/E6 verification. End with Kisin1.2.21/1.2.23: rational Tate-lattice modifications of an adapted lift meet every frame component. Unit tests must distinguish invariants from coinvariants, orbit norms from invariant lifts and rational κ from torsion κ. Correction: the proof of Proposition (1.2.21) needs the replacement argument through π_1 when Z_G is disconnected (E20).

routes.brief: Reuse the global reductive-arithmetic candidate of KMPS22 and Kisin–Zhou25. Import reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1/AA.3/AA.4), global number fields (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields), ET.0 reductive cohomology, SF.1 gerb foundations, and Néron models and semistable abelian varieties (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties) for connected torus Néron models. Build Q_L, weighted trace relations, norm-power transitions, local fundamental gerbs, the quasi-motivic gerb and universal ψ before the Weil tori P^L, their Frobenius elements and pushout gerb P. This constructs the gerb used by the paper and assumes no motivic realization conjecture; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC6 remains its own Tannakian owner. Give the Serre-cocharacter condition both Galois identities and its split-times-compact consequence. Prove toric local/adelic parameter trivialization with connected T° level and inertia coinvariants; prove sufficiently divisible reciprocity and gerb Frobenius constructions agree already at a finite unramified level. The endpoint includes Kisin2.2.2 cocharacter selection,3.1.9 gerb existence/uniqueness,3.5.3 Weil trace property,3.6.7 toric trivialization and4.3.11 toric triple agreement. Original Langlands–Rapoport, Milne, class-field and approximation proofs remain explicit closure obligations. Corrections: (3.3.2) defines a strictly monoidal ψ_μ only after μ is moved into a Q-torus (E42); the proof of Lemma (3.2.4) needs the torsion argument (E40).

routes.brief: Reuse the KMPS22/Kisin–Zhou25/KPZ26/KP18 integral-reduction candidate. Import Shimura varieties (ShimuraVarieties), Shimura data (ShimuraData), PEL moduli (PELModuli), abelian-scheme twisting (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli), every local/gerb/cohomology owner listed in this extraction and AdelicAlgebraicGroups for approximation. First prove the Hodge integral isogeny map and frame-family propagation with tensor branches, then every isogeny class has a special lift (Kisin2.2.3) and tensor automorphisms match all local Frobenius centralizers. Stabilize geometric endomorphisms using sufficiently divisible fields. Build refined G/Gsc admissibility, special morphisms, local parameter torsors, component identifications and arithmetic Frobenius extensions; these import generic gerb and nonabelian cohomology rather than defining them privately. Build torsor twists of geometric classes and gerb morphisms, stabilized Kottwitz triples, adelic refinements, and the two Sha_G torsor-fiber theorems4.4.13/4.5.7. Match special torus triples, adjust components using J_b, and choose the adelic tau matching the actions. Prove4.6.2/4.6.5 with torus center, then the permitted Hodge-derived cover and central-isogeny descent. The final theorem4.6.7 is a Frobenius, center and A(G2)-equivariant point-tower bijection for p>2, abelian type and hyperspecial level with I(Q) action twisted by tau∈Iad(Af) depending only on the adjoint morphism class. It is not an untwisted LR theorem or a geometric-space isomorphism. Keep3.3.7/3.7.8 as conjecture predicates. Apply the integral-model errata: Δ° can be infinite; prove finite action at suitable levels before inverse-limit descent. Preserve real positivity, topological closures, Serre-center assumptions and conjugated levels throughout. Corrections the design must carry: define X̃^p(φ) in (3.6.1) with ε_l unramified for almost all l, without which Lemma 3.6.2(2),(3), Corollary 3.6.4 and Proposition 3.6.10 fail when G^der is not simply connected (E53); Corollary (2.3.5) needs k large or the groups I_{/k}, I_{l/k} (E34); Corollary 3.8.6 must include the reflex degree r (E70); Theorem 4.6.7 needs p > 2 (E104); the κ-step in the proof of Lemma 4.5.6 fails when π_1(G)_Γ has torsion and is replaced by the argument of (3.4.2) (E98).

Printed (as footnote 8 reports it): 𝔐(𝒢) := 𝔐(T_p𝒢*) and L = T_p𝒢*. Correction: replace T_p𝒢* by T_p𝒢*(−1) = Hom_{Z_p}(T_p𝒢, Z_p) in all three, as this paper does in (1.1.6)–(1.1.7). sourceIssues.reason: The contravariant Dieudonné crystal D(𝒢) corresponds under the p-adic comparison to the dual T_p𝒢^∨ = T_p𝒢*(−1) (Weil pairing T_p𝒢 × T_p𝒢* → Z_p(1)). With T_p𝒢* the Galois module is off by a Tate twist, so the comparison D(𝒢)(S) ≅ ℳ(𝔐(·)) and the statements built on it are misstated in [Ki 2]. The extraction's source issues (E1–E5) do not record this printed correction.

review.reason: The mistake is in [Ki 2], not in this paper. It is a correction made in print by the author, like E1–E4. The image of footnote 8 (p. 7) reads: 'In fact T_p𝒢* should be replaced by T_p𝒢*(−1), the linear dual of T_p𝒢, in (1.4.2), (1.4.3) and (1.5.11) of loc. cit. We have made this correction here.' The claim's `printed` is not text from this paper. It paraphrases [Ki 2], and its locator should name [Ki 2]. I could not reach the published [Ki 2] (the AMS site returns a Cloudflare page). Kisin's homepage has the author's corrected version of [Ki 2] (shimcorrpub.dvi, footnote: 'This version corrects some mistakes in the published version'). There Thm 1.4.2 reads 𝒢 ↦ 𝔐(𝒢) := 𝔐(T_p𝒢*(−1)), and Cor 1.4.3 and Cor 1.5.11 read L = T_p𝒢*(−1): exactly the three places footnote 8 names. The mathematics: the Weil pairing gives T_p𝒢* ≅ Hom(T_p𝒢, Z_p(1)), so T_p𝒢*(−1) = T_p𝒢^∨. The contravariant crystal D(𝒢) corresponds to V_p𝒢^∨, whose filtration jumps lie in {0,1}, the range of BT^φ_{/𝔖}. With T_p𝒢* the jumps lie in {−1,0}. For 𝒢 = Q_p/Z_p, T_p𝒢* = Z_p(1) is not even in that range. For 𝒢 = μ_{p^∞}, 𝔐(T_p𝒢*) = 𝔐(Z_p) has Fil^1ℳ = Fil^1S·ℳ, whereas Fil^1 D(μ_{p^∞})(S) is all of D(μ_{p^∞})(S). So the printed (1.4.2) of [Ki 2], D(𝒢)(S) ≅ ℳ(𝔐(T_p𝒢*)), is false. The footnote's own correction is right, and this paper uses T_p𝒢*(−1) throughout ((1.1.6), (1.1.7), (1.1.13), (1.2.16)–(1.2.18)). E1–E5 do not record it, and `known` (corrected in print, footnote 8) is accurate.

(1.1.19) proof: 'these tensors define a connected reductive subgroup in GL(T_p𝒢̃′). Hence by (1.1.7), there exist W-linear isomorphisms (1.1.21)'; 'Since μ′_0 and gμ_0g^{-1} are G^g_W-valued cocharacters, they are conjugate by an element of G^g_W(W).'
sourceIssues.correction: In (1.1.13), make the last sentence read: 'If this condition holds and G_{Z_p} is connected (or k is separably closed), then there exists a W-linear isomorphism (1.1.14)'. Prove it from U, not from [Ki 2, 1.4.3(3)]. Isom((U,s_{α,0}), (T_p𝒢̃*(−1), s_α)) is a G_{Z_p}-torsor over Z_p, split over W(k^sep) by [Ki 2, 1.4.3(2)], hence trivial by Lang and Hensel. In (1.1.19), assume G_{Z_p} connected or k separably closed. For connected G and general k, obtain (1.1.21) from Nisnevich's theorem, since the torsor is trivial over K_0 via D(θ).
sourceIssues.reason: Throughout §1.1, k is an arbitrary perfect field (1.1.1), and neither (1.1.13) nor (1.1.19) restricts it. Their proofs rest on (1.1.7) = [Ki 2, 1.4.3], which the paper states only under 'k separably closed, or G_{Z_p} connected and k finite'. (The proof cites [Ki 2, 1.4.3(3)]. In (1.1.7), which restates [Ki 2, 1.4.3], the isomorphism is part (2) and part (3) is the filtration statement, so the part number in the cross-reference may also be off; not checkable without [Ki 2].) For general perfect k the relevant G_W-torsors (tensor-preserving isomorphisms, and transporters between conjugate cocharacters) need not be trivial over W(k), since H^1(k, ·) can be non-zero. In (1.1.19) connectedness of the stabiliser is asserted without argument (it follows only if G_{Z_p} is connected). Defence: when G_{Z_p} is connected, the Z_p-structure U shows that the isomorphism scheme in (1.1.13) is a torsor over Z_p, hence trivial by Lang and Hensel for any k. So the gap concerns disconnected G_{Z_p}, and the steps in (1.1.19) that do not come from U, over non-separably-closed k.

review.reason: The problem is real, and it is worse than a gap: for disconnected G_{Z_p} the last sentence of (1.1.13) is false. In §1.1, 'reductive' allows disconnected groups: (1.1.4)(2) and (1.1.7) state 'G connected' as a separate hypothesis, and [Ki 2, §1.1] defines a reductive group as G with G/G^0 finite étale. Nothing restricts k beyond being perfect (1.1.1). Counterexample, with p odd, k = F_p (so W = Z_p and K = Q_p). Let 𝒢̃ be the étale p-divisible group over Z_p whose T := T_p𝒢̃*(−1) ≅ Z_p^2 has Frobenius acting by the swap τ. Take the tensors v = e_1+e_2 and the form x^2+y^2, whose stabiliser is the finite étale group {1,τ}. That group is reductive in Kisin's sense and contains the Galois image, so the tensors are G_K-invariant. Take U = D(𝒢)(Z_p) = (T ⊗ W(F̄_p))^{τ⊗σ}, with s_{α,0} the images of s_α. The hypotheses of (1.1.11)–(1.1.13) hold: the filtration is trivial, and 𝒢̃ is G_W-adapted. But the isomorphisms (D(𝒢)(Z_p), s_{α,0}) → (T, s_α) form the {1,τ}-torsor with class τ ≠ 0 in H^1(F_p, Z/2), so no isomorphism (1.1.14) exists. The proof cites [Ki 2, 1.4.3(3)], which assumes 'G connected and k finite'. I checked the author's corrected version of [Ki 2], which is all I could reach: there 1.4.3 has four parts, and (3) is precisely the W-linear isomorphism under that hypothesis. So the part number is right, and the claim's aside that it 'may also be off' should be dropped. For connected G_{Z_p} the statement holds for every perfect k, but the proof does not show it for infinite k. The fix: the isomorphism scheme U → T_p𝒢̃*(−1) respecting tensors is a G_{Z_p}-torsor over Z_p, trivial over W(k^sep) by [Ki 2, 1.4.3(2)], hence trivial by Lang and Hensel. (1.1.19) has the same defect. 'these tensors define a connected reductive subgroup' is false when G_{Z_p} is disconnected, and the appeal to (1.1.7) needs its hypotheses. For connected G it can be repaired at any perfect k. The isomorphism for 𝒢′ is a G_W-torsor over W that is trivial over K_0 via D(θ), hence trivial by Nisnevich (Grothendieck–Serre over a DVR). The conjugacy of μ′_0 and gμ_0g^{-1} over W follows from the injectivity of H^1(k,P) → H^1(k,G) and Hensel. No later result is affected. The uses in (1.2.15)–(1.2.19) have k = F̄_p. §1.3 and §2 (including (2.2.3)) have G_{Z_p} connected.

review.reason: Checked on the image of p. 10. From c = σ^{-1}(b)μ_0(E(0)) and the identity σ(λ(x)) = (σλ)(σx) for a cocharacter λ over W, σ(c) = b·(σμ_0)(σ(E(0))) = b·υ_0(σ(E(0)))^{-1}, since υ_0 = σ(μ_0^{-1}). E(0) is ±N_{K/K_0}(π) ∈ W and is σ-fixed only when it lies in Z_p (e.g. k = F_p). This choice of c is the right one: at u = 0 it gives cμ_0(E(0))^{-1} = σ^{-1}(b), so the Frobenius on φ*(𝔐)/u is bσ. The slip is harmless. σ(E(0)) and E(0) are both p times a unit, so υ_0(p/σ(E(0))) ∈ G_W(W). Also bυ_0(p)^{-1} = h_1h_2 ∈ G_W(W) by the proof of (1.1.12). Hence c ∈ G_W(W) ⊂ GL(D(𝒢)(W)), which also keeps the s_{α,0} φ-invariant in 𝔐.

review.reason: (4) is false as stated, already for i = 0. Take the crossed module ∂ = 1: Z/3 → Z/2 with Z/2 acting on Z/3 by inversion (its cokernel Z/2 is abelian), and let Δ = Z/3 act trivially. The canonical product coming from the monoidal structure of (3.2.1) is (a,h)(a′,h′) = (a + h·a′, hh′). So H^0 ≅ Z/3 ⋊ Z/2 = S_3, which is non-abelian. The first reading's H^1 example with Z/4 illustrates the same failure. A canonical abelian structure needs a braided (Picard) structure, which forces π0 to act trivially on π1, or a quasi-isomorphism to a complex of abelian groups as in [Bo]. Every application in the paper is covered: (4.4.2) for H̃ → H with H reductive, and Z_{G̃} → Z_G, both via [Bo, 3.8].

review.reason: Admissibility for the auxiliary (G,X) needs the standing hypothesis of (3.3.6), namely a reductive model G_{Z_p}, because X_p(φ) is defined using G_{Z_p}(Z_p^ur). So do 3.4.11 and [LR, Satz 5.3], which works at hyperspecial level. If L is ramified at p, S_L and hence G = (H̃×S_L^n)/Z_{H̃} are ramified at p, and none of this applies. The proof never says L must be unramified at p, but the choice is always possible. H is unramified, so inertia at p acts trivially on its Dynkin diagram, and the field K it cuts out is unramified at p; K is CM or totally real. If K is totally real, then c acts trivially on X^*(Z_{H̃}), which is therefore 2-torsion. One can then use L = K(√−d) with Q(√−d) unramified at p (d = 1 for p odd, d = 3 for p = 2). Then S_L is an unramified torus, and G has a reductive Z_p-model. Also confirmed on the page: 'Hence the lemma holds' should be 'the theorem holds', and 𝕊_0 is used without definition (it should be the weight G_{m,R} ⊂ 𝕊). The lift h̃ exists because the extension of the compact 𝕊/G_m by the compact torus Z_{G,R} splits: Ext^1 of Z(−1) by Z(−1) over Z[Gal(C/R)] is 0.

sourceIssues.reason: Lang's lemma trivializes only unramified cocycles, and the integrality condition does not exclude ramified ones. Suppose ker(ρ: G̃ → G) ≠ 1, the non-simply-connected case the section is for. Take (g_l,ε_l) ∈ X̃^p(φ) and replace ε_l by ε_l·c_l, where c_l ∈ Z^1(Q_l, ker ρ) is ramified for infinitely many l (such classes exist by Tate duality and Chebotarev; e.g. G = PGL_2, c_l the quadratic character of Q_l(√l)). Every printed condition still holds, because c_l takes values in the finite central group ker ρ ⊂ G̃(Z̄_l). Suppose this family were h·(x·γ) with h ∈ G̃(Ā^p_f) and γ ∈ G(A^p_f). Then k_l := g_l^{-1}⋆h_l would satisfy ρ(k_l) = γ_l^{-1} and k_l^{-1}τ(k_l) = c_l, so γ_l ∈ G^der(Q_l) and δ(γ_l^{-1}) = [c_l] ∈ H^1(Q_l, ker ρ). But γ_l ∈ G^der(Z_l) for almost all l, and δ(G^der(Z_l)) is unramified for l ∤ |ker ρ|. So X^p(φ_ab~) is not a single G(A^p_f)/G̃(A^p_f)-orbit, and as literally defined π(G,φ_0) is not a π(G)-torsor (3.6.2(2),(3), 3.6.4, 3.6.10). In the paper's defence, the intended object (a restricted product) is clear, and only the definition needs changing.

review.reason: Quotations checked on pp.52, 54 (text and fn.20). The page-54 text drops the tildes: it says G_{Z_l}(Z̄_l) and G(Ā^p_f). I tried to show that the paper's own definitions rule out the counterexample. They do not. (i) The only global condition in (3.6.1) is that the values ε_l(τ_l) lie in G̃(Ā^p_f). That constrains the values of ε_l, not whether ε_l is ramified. (ii) Let c_l ∈ Z^1(Q_l, ker ρ) with ker ρ = ker(G̃→G^der), a finite central group. The twisted action (conjugation through G^ad) is trivial on ker ρ. So ε_l·c_l is again a cocycle, and ρ(ε_lc_l) = ρ(ε_l). The pair also gives a morphism in the crossed-module category of (3.2.1), since Hom(h_1,h_2) = {h̃ : h_2 = h̃h_1}. For almost all l, ker ρ(Q̄_l) lies in G̃_{Z_l}(Z̄_l), because ker ρ is finite over Z_l. So (g_l, ε_lc_l) ∈ X̃^p(φ). (iii) Suppose (g_l,1) ∈ X̃^p(φ_ab~) comes from X^p(φ), and suppose (g_l, c_l) = k·(g_lγ_l, 1) with γ ∈ G(A^p_f) and k_l ∈ G̃(Q̄_l); I do not even require k to be integral at almost all l. Put k′_l = (g_lγ_l)^{-1}⋆k_l. Then ρ(k′_l) = γ_l^{-1} and τ(k′_l)k′_l^{-1} = c_l. So γ_l ∈ G^der(Q_l) and δ(γ_l^{-1}) = ±[c_l] ∈ H^1(Q_l, ker ρ). For almost all l, γ_l ∈ G(Z_l) ∩ G^der(Q_l) = G^der(Z_l), whose δ-image consists of unramified classes when l ∤ |ker ρ|. For example, take G = PGL_2 (a Shimura datum with hyperspecial level at any p) and c_l the character of Q_l(√l) for odd l ≠ p. Then δ = det mod squares, and l is never in Z_l^×·Q_l^{×2}. So the class is not in g_0·G(A_f). (iv) The classes that are adelically trivial (those of (g_l,1)) form a subset stable under G(A_f), under G(Q̄)^♮_+ (which acts by right multiplication on the g_l and leaves ε unchanged), and under K^p. Using G(Q)_+ instead of G(Q̄)^♮_+ does not help: in the paper's convention the subscript + means the preimage of G^ad(R)^+, and G(Q̄)^♮_+ ∩ G(Q) = G(Q)_+ ⊂ G(A_f). So the extra classes are never identified with g_0·G(A_f) at any level K^p. Hence for G^der ≠ G̃, taking X^p(φ_ab~) literally makes (3.6.2)(2) non-surjective and (3.6.2)(3) not a bijection. Then π(G,φ_0) is not a π(G)-torsor, so (3.6.4) and (3.6.10) fail as stated, and so does the surjectivity of c_G in (3.7.4). Footnote 20 shows that the author had unramified ε_l in mind. The intended object is clear, and only the definition needs changing.

review.reason: Checked on p.77. By (4.3.1), I_l = Cent(γ_l^n) for n large, and β(τ) ∈ I_l(Q̄_l) via ι. This can be strictly larger than Cent(γ_l). Example: a supersingular elliptic curve over F_p with π^2 = −p; γ_0 = π has a torus as centralizer, while γ_0^2 is central, so I_0 = GL_2. Then β(τ) need not commute with γ_l, and τ(γ_l^β) = γ_l^β fails. The same issue affects the next claim, that g_l is determined up to right multiplication by I(Q̄_l) and so γ_l^β up to G(Q_l)-conjugacy. The fix is to use a representative whose own γ_l has centralizer I_l. The equivalence relation allows this, but the text chooses the representative only at p ('After increasing the finite field k'). Lemma 4.3.7 is affected only through the definition of k^β. Once k^β is defined this way, both directions go through, because conjugacy of sufficiently divisible powers suffices and Cent(γ_l) ⊂ I_l.

review.reason: Checked on p.83. The claim is correct. The proof shows that I_x^β stays in the fibre ((4.3.7), (4.4.11)), that β ↦ I_x^β is injective for a fixed base point ((4.4.8)), and transitivity. It never checks that I_y ↦ I_y^β is a group action. That needs: for each y in the fibre, the identification Ш_G(Q,I_y) ≅ Ш_G(Q,I) ((4.4.3)); independence of the base point within an isogeny class; and (I_y^β)^{β'} = I_y^{β+β'}. These are true. By the proof of (4.4.8), y ∈ I_x^β iff the torsor of tensor-preserving quasi-isogenies A_y → A_x has class β. Composing torsors is the twisting map, which is translation by β on Ш^∞, abelian via (4.4.2). But this argument appears nowhere in the paper, and the 'torsor' clause of Prop. 4.4.13 depends on it. So the proof, not just the exposition, is incomplete. The counting later needs only the bijection for a fixed base point, and the stated result is true, so affects = the proof, not nothing.

review.reason: Checked on p.90. The printed identification π_1(R_{F/Q_p}G)_Γ = π_1(G)_Γ ⊗ Z[Gal(F/Q_p)] is wrong. Over Q̄_p, R_{F/Q_p}G is the product of copies of G indexed by Hom(F,Q̄_p), and Γ permutes these factors while also acting on π_1(G). So π_1(R_{F/Q_p}G) = Ind_{Γ_F}^{Γ} π_1(G), whose Γ-coinvariants are π_1(G)_{Γ_F} (Shapiro's lemma). The diagonal G → R_{F/Q_p}G induces the transfer π_1(G)_Γ → π_1(G)_{Γ_F}, x ↦ Σ_{Γ/Γ_F} g·x. This is multiplication by e for F totally ramified of degree e, and 1+σ+…+σ^{f−1} for F = Q_{p^f}. Composing with the projection back to π_1(G)_Γ gives multiplication by [F:Q_p], so only torsion can be lost, but torsion can be lost. Counterexample: T = U(1) for Q_{p^2}/Q_p, F = Q_{p^2}. Then X_*(T)_Γ = Z/2 and X_*(T)_{Γ_F} = Z, and the map is x ↦ x+σx = 0. Twisting δ = 1 by the nontrivial class of H^1(Q_p,T) = Z/2 (which splits over Q_{p^2}) gives δ' = h_0σ(h_0)^{-1} with κ_T(δ') ≠ 0 = κ_T(δ), although both have the same image in π_1(R_{F/Q_p}T)_Γ. The same happens for GU(V) with dim V even and p inert, where π_1(G)_Γ ⊃ Z/2 is killed by F = Q_{p^2}. The printed step never uses the hypothesis on β at p, so it would 'prove' that every local twist preserves κ_G, which is false. The conclusion κ_G(h_0δσ(h_0)^{-1}) = κ_G(δ) is still true under the lemma's hypotheses. The first paragraph of the proof shows that φ^β = z·φ satisfies (3.3.6)(1), and the κ-part of the proof of (3.4.2) ((3.4.4) pushed to π_1(G) ≅ X_*(G/G̃)) uses only (3.3.6)(1). It gives κ_G = −μ^♮ for the element attached to the unramified conjugate (z·φ)(p)_{g_0h̄_0^{-1}}. So Lemma 4.5.6 and the results that use it (4.5.7, 4.5.11, 4.6.2) stand.
